source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including written/read and other notes; no normalized reconstruction.
source.public_versification_note: All titles are inside public verse 1. Psalms 65, 67, 68, 69, 70, 75, 76, 77, 80, 81, 83, 84, 85, 88, 89, 92, 102 bind one separate title record plus Hebrew verse 2 to public verse 1; following labels are offset by one. Other selected labels match. All 763 original source records bind exactly once, including every note; no source record is partitioned in this batch.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial choices are independent of overlap scores. No minimum-change quota. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Retain silence beside praise, noting difficult relation; include separate title.
verses.before: Silence and praise await you, God, in Zion; and to you vows will be fulfilled.
verses.after: For the music leader. A psalm of David. A song. God, praise waits in silence for you in Zion; to you the vow will be fulfilled.
verses.tsw_comparator: Silence and praise await you, God, in Zion; and to you vows shall be fulfilled.

verses.rationale: Keep bodily universal scope and direct address.
verses.before: O you who hear prayer, to you all flesh will come.
verses.after: You who hear prayer, all flesh will come to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: O you who hear prayer, to you all flesh will come.

verses.rationale: Preserve singular me to plural our and atonement verb.
verses.before: Words of iniquities prevail against me; our transgressions—you atone for them.
verses.after: Wrongdoings have overwhelmed me, but you atone for our rebellions.
verses.tsw_comparator: Words of iniquities prevail against me; our transgressions—you atone for them.

verses.rationale: Retain choosing, approach, residence and communal satisfaction.
verses.before: Happy are those whom you choose and bring near, to dwell in your courts! We will be satisfied with the goodness of your house, the holiness of your temple.
verses.after: Happy is the one you choose and bring near to live in your courts! Let us be filled with the goodness of your house, your holy temple.
verses.tsw_comparator: Happy are those whom you choose and bring near, to dwell in your courts! We shall be satisfied with the goodness of your house, the holiness of your temple.

verses.rationale: Keep cosmic scope and righteous answer, not private assurance only.
verses.before: With awe-inspiring deeds of righteousness you answer us, O God of our salvation, the hope of all the ends of the earth and of the distant seas.
verses.after: With awesome deeds of righteousness you answer us, God who saves us, the trust of all the earth’s farthest reaches and the distant seas.
verses.tsw_comparator: With awe-inspiring deeds of righteousness you answer us, O God of our salvation, the hope of all the ends of the earth and of the distant seas.

verses.rationale: Continue direct address while preserving girding metaphor.
verses.before: You set the mountains in place by your strength, being girded with might;
verses.after: You establish mountains by your power, clothed with might.
verses.tsw_comparator: You set the mountains in place by your strength, being girded with might;

verses.rationale: Repeat roar and parallel natural/social turbulence.
verses.before: Who calms the roaring of the seas, the roaring of their waves, and the tumult of the peoples.
verses.after: You still the roar of seas, the roar of their waves, and the tumult of peoples.
verses.tsw_comparator: Who calms the roaring of the seas, the roaring of their waves, and the tumult of the peoples.

verses.rationale: Keep geographical horizons rejoicing rather than merely times of day.
verses.before: People who dwell at the farthest ends are in awe of your signs; you make the dawn and the sunset shout for joy.
verses.after: Those who live at earth’s edges stand in awe of your signs. You make the places of sunrise and sunset shout for joy.
verses.tsw_comparator: Those who dwell at the farthest ends are in awe of your signs; you make the dawn and the sunset shout for joy.

verses.rationale: Retain third-person God within address and doubled preparation.
verses.before: You visit the earth and water it, you greatly enrich it; the river of God is full of water; you prepare their grain, for so you provide for it.
verses.after: You attend to the earth and water it, enriching it greatly. God’s stream is full of water. You prepare their grain, for this is how you prepare the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: You visit the earth and water it, you greatly enrich it; the river of God is full of water; you prepare their grain, for so you provide for it.

verses.rationale: Preserve sequence of cultivation and rain.
verses.before: You drench its furrows, smooth its ridges, you soften it with showers, and bless its growth.
verses.after: You soak its furrows and settle its ridges, soften it with showers and bless its growth.
verses.tsw_comparator: You drench its furrows, smooth its ridges, you soften it with showers, and bless its growth.

verses.rationale: Keep crown and tracks, not a generic prosperous year.
verses.before: You crown the year with your bounty; your carts overflow with abundance.
verses.after: You crown the year with your goodness; your tracks drip with abundance.
verses.tsw_comparator: You crown the year with your bounty; your carts overflow with abundance.

verses.rationale: Continue abundance and clothing imagery.
verses.before: The pastures of the wilderness overflow, and the hills gird themselves with joy;
verses.after: The wilderness pastures drip with it; the hills wrap themselves in joy.
verses.tsw_comparator: The pastures of the wilderness overflow, and the hills gird themselves with joy;

verses.rationale: Keep land clothed and singing, not replace with human praise.
verses.before: The meadows clothe themselves with flocks, the valleys deck themselves with grain; they shout and sing together for joy.
verses.after: The meadows put on flocks; the valleys clothe themselves in grain. They shout for joy—yes, they sing!
verses.tsw_comparator: The meadows clothe themselves with flocks, the valleys deck themselves with grain; they shout and sing together for joy.

verses.rationale: Inline title retained with universal call.
verses.before: Make a joyful shout to God, all the earth.
verses.after: For the music leader. A song. A psalm. Shout to God, all the earth!
verses.tsw_comparator: Make a joyful shout to God, all the earth.

verses.rationale: Retain repeated glory and name.
verses.before: Sing the glory of his name; give glory to his praise.
verses.after: Make music to the glory of his name; make his praise glorious.
verses.tsw_comparator: Sing the glory of his name; give glory to his praise.

verses.rationale: Feigning submission rather than willing conversion.
verses.before: Say to God, “How fearsome are your works. Because of the greatness of your strength, your enemies cringe before you.
verses.after: Say to God, “How awesome are your deeds! Before your great strength, your enemies cringe.
verses.tsw_comparator: Say to God, “How fearsome are your works. Because of the greatness of your strength, your enemies cringe before you.

verses.rationale: Preserve three acts and close quoted address.
verses.before: All the earth bows down to you and sings to you; they sing praise to your name.”
verses.after: All the earth bows before you and makes music to you; they make music to your name.” Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the earth bows down to you and sings to you; they sing praise to your name.”

verses.rationale: Invitation shifts from speaking to seeing.
verses.before: Come and see the works of God; fearsome is his doing toward the children of humankind.
verses.after: Come and see what God has done, his awesome dealings with humanity.
verses.tsw_comparator: Come and see the works of God; fearsome is his doing toward the children of humankind.

verses.rationale: Keep sea and river distinct and past-to-present communal participation.
verses.before: He turned the sea into dry ground; through the river they passed on foot. There we rejoiced in him,
verses.after: He turned the sea into dry ground; they crossed the river on foot. There let us rejoice in him!
verses.tsw_comparator: He turned the sea into dry ground; through the river they passed on foot. There we rejoiced in him,

verses.rationale: Follow read rise, retaining warning.
verses.before: who rules by his strength forever, whose eyes keep watch on the nations. Let the rebellious not exalt themselves.
verses.after: He rules forever by his might; his eyes watch the nations. Let the rebellious not exalt themselves. Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: who rules by his strength forever, whose eyes keep watch on the nations. Let the rebellious not exalt themselves.

verses.rationale: International summons and audible praise.
verses.before: Bless our God, O peoples; let the sound of his praise be heard,
verses.after: Bless our God, you peoples; let the sound of his praise be heard.
verses.tsw_comparator: Bless our God, O peoples; let the sound of his praise be heard,

verses.rationale: Keep life and stable-foot image.
verses.before: who has kept our soul among the living and has not let our foot slip.
verses.after: He has kept us among the living and has not let our feet slip.
verses.tsw_comparator: who has kept our soul among the living and has not let our foot slip.

verses.rationale: Retain repeated refining process.
verses.before: For you, O God, have tested us; you have refined us as silver is refined.
verses.after: You tested us, God; you refined us as silver is refined.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you, O God, have tested us; you have refined us as silver is refined.

verses.rationale: Net plus burden remain distinct trials from God.
verses.before: You brought us into the net; you laid a crushing burden on our backs.
verses.after: You brought us into a net; you laid a crushing load on our backs.
verses.tsw_comparator: You brought us into the net; you laid a crushing burden on our backs.

verses.rationale: Preserve violent subjection and contrasting emergence.
verses.before: You let mortals ride over our heads; we went through fire and through water, yet you brought us out to a place of abundance.
verses.after: You let people ride over our heads. We went through fire and water, but you brought us out into abundance.
verses.tsw_comparator: You let mortals ride over our heads; we went through fire and through water, yet you brought us out to a place of abundance.

verses.rationale: Communal voice becomes singular without invented speaker identity.
verses.before: I will come into your house with burnt offerings; I will pay you my vows,
verses.after: I will enter your house with burnt offerings and fulfill my vows to you—
verses.tsw_comparator: I will come into your house with burnt offerings; I will pay you my vows,

verses.rationale: Continue vow sentence with distress occasion.
verses.before: which my lips uttered and my mouth spoke when I was in distress.
verses.after: the vows my lips uttered and my mouth spoke when I was in distress.
verses.tsw_comparator: which my lips uttered and my mouth spoke when I was in distress.

verses.rationale: All animal classes and offering smoke retained.
verses.before: I will offer to you burnt offerings of fatlings, with the smoke of rams; I will make an offering of bulls with goats.
verses.after: I will offer you fat animals as burnt offerings, with the smoke of rams; I will sacrifice cattle and male goats. Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will offer to you burnt offerings of fatlings, with the smoke of rams; I will make an offering of bulls with goats.

verses.rationale: Hearing invitation answers seeing invitation.
verses.before: Come and hear, all you who fear God, and I will tell what he has done for my soul.
verses.after: Come and hear, all who revere God; I will tell what he has done for me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Come and hear, all you who fear God, and I will tell what he has done for my soul.

verses.rationale: Under tongue idiom clarified in note.
verses.before: I cried to him with my mouth, and praise was under my tongue.
verses.after: My mouth called to him; high praise was ready on my tongue.
verses.tsw_comparator: I cried to him with my mouth, and praise was under my tongue.

verses.rationale: Conditional claim kept, not general theory of unanswered prayer.
verses.before: If I had regarded iniquity in my heart, the Lord would not have listened.
verses.after: Had I cherished wrongdoing in my heart, the Lord would not have listened.
verses.tsw_comparator: If I had regarded iniquity in my heart, the Lord would not have listened.

verses.rationale: Emphatic actual hearing contrasts counterfactual.
verses.before: But truly God has listened; he has attended to the voice of my prayer.
verses.after: But God did listen; he paid attention to my prayer’s voice.
verses.tsw_comparator: But truly God has listened; he has attended to the voice of my prayer.

verses.rationale: Preserve prayer/love double object with natural different verbs.
verses.before: Blessed be God, who has not turned away my prayer or his steadfast love from me.
verses.after: Blessed be God, who has not turned away my prayer or withdrawn his faithful love from me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Blessed be God, who has not turned away my prayer or his steadfast love from me.

verses.rationale: Separate title and blessing face retained.
verses.before: May God be gracious to us and bless us and make his face shine upon us,
verses.after: For the music leader. With stringed instruments. A psalm. A song. May God be gracious to us and bless us; may he make his face shine upon us. Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: May God be gracious to us and bless us and make his face shine upon us,

verses.rationale: Blessing purpose extends beyond us.
verses.before: that your way may be known on earth, your saving power among all nations.
verses.after: Then your way will be known on earth, your salvation among all nations.
verses.tsw_comparator: that your way may be known on earth, your saving power among all nations.

verses.rationale: Exact doubled communal refrain.
verses.before: Let the peoples praise you, O God; let all the peoples praise you!
verses.after: Let the peoples thank you, God; let all the peoples thank you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let the peoples praise you, O God; let all the peoples praise you!

verses.rationale: Justice and guidance ground gladness.
verses.before: Let the nations be glad and sing for joy, for you judge the peoples with equity and guide the nations upon the earth.
verses.after: Let nations rejoice and sing aloud, for you judge peoples fairly and guide the nations on earth. Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let the nations be glad and sing for joy, for you judge the peoples with equity and guide the nations upon the earth.

verses.rationale: Repeat verse 3 unchanged.
verses.before: Let the peoples praise you, O God; let all the peoples praise you!
verses.after: Let the peoples thank you, God; let all the peoples thank you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let the peoples praise you, O God; let all the peoples praise you!

verses.rationale: Harvest perfect and blessing wish distinguished.
verses.before: The earth has yielded its increase; God, our God, will bless us.
verses.after: The earth has yielded its harvest; may God, our God, bless us.
verses.tsw_comparator: The earth has yielded its increase; God, our God, shall bless us.

verses.rationale: Concluding blessing again universal in reach.
verses.before: God will bless us; let all the ends of the earth fear him!
verses.after: May God bless us, and may all the ends of the earth revere him.
verses.tsw_comparator: God shall bless us; let all the ends of the earth fear him!

verses.rationale: Keep three energetic petitions and title.
verses.before: God arises, his enemies are scattered; people who hate him flee before him.
verses.after: For the music leader. Of David. A psalm. A song. Let God rise! Let his enemies scatter; let those who hate him flee from his presence.
verses.tsw_comparator: God arises, his enemies are scattered; those who hate him flee before him.

verses.rationale: Direct command within smoke/wax similes retained.
verses.before: As smoke is driven away, so you drive them away; as wax melts before fire, so the wicked perish before God.
verses.after: As smoke is driven away, drive them away; as wax melts before fire, let the wicked perish before God.
verses.tsw_comparator: As smoke is driven away, so you drive them away; as wax melts before fire, so the wicked perish before God.

verses.rationale: Retain cumulative joy without flattening repetition.
verses.before: But the righteous are glad; they exult before God; they rejoice with gladness.
verses.after: But let the righteous be glad and exult before God; let them rejoice with joy.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the righteous are glad; they exult before God; they rejoice with gladness.

verses.rationale: Aravot wilderness chosen with cloud alternative noted; YAH short name preserved.
verses.before: Sing to God, sing praises to his name; lift up a song to him who rides through the deserts; his name is the LORD— exult before him.
verses.after: Sing to God; make music to his name. Build a road for the rider through the wilderness. His name is YAH; rejoice before him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Sing to God, sing praises to his name; lift up a song to him who rides through the deserts; his name is the LORD— exult before him.

verses.rationale: Keep social roles, not generic kindness.
verses.before: Father of the fatherless and judge of widows is God in his holy dwelling.
verses.after: A father to orphans, a judge for widows— God in his holy dwelling.
verses.tsw_comparator: Father of the fatherless and judge of widows is God in his holy dwelling.

verses.rationale: Rare prosperity term acknowledged, home/release/dryness contrast.
verses.before: God settles the solitary in a home; he leads out the prisoners to prosperity, but the rebellious dwell in a parched land.
verses.after: God settles the lonely in a home and brings prisoners out into prosperity; but rebels live in a parched land.
verses.tsw_comparator: God settles the solitary in a home; he leads out the prisoners to prosperity, but the rebellious dwell in a parched land.

verses.rationale: Keep dependent sentence across verse break.
verses.before: O God, when you went out before your people, when you marched through the wilderness,
verses.after: God, when you went out before your people, when you marched through the wasteland, Selah,
verses.tsw_comparator: O God, when you went out before your people, when you marched through the wilderness,

verses.rationale: Preserve difficult Sinai phrase and repeated before God.
verses.before: the earth quaked, the heavens also poured down rain at the presence of God, this Sinai at the presence of God, the God of Israel.
verses.after: the earth shook, the heavens poured rain before God—the one of Sinai— before God, the God of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: the earth quaked, the heavens also poured down rain at the presence of God, this Sinai at the presence of God, the God of Israel.

verses.rationale: Land inheritance weariness and replenishment retained.
verses.before: Rain in abundance, O God, you poured out; you restored your inheritance when it languished;
verses.after: You showered abundant rain, God; when your inheritance was weary, you restored it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Rain in abundance, O God, you poured out; you restored your inheritance when it languished;

verses.rationale: Hayyah flock/community ambiguity noted, poor provision preserved.
verses.before: your flock found a dwelling in it; in your goodness, O God, you provided for the needy.
verses.after: Your flock settled there; in your goodness, God, you provided for the afflicted.
verses.tsw_comparator: your flock found a dwelling in it; in your goodness, O God, you provided for the needy.

verses.rationale: Explicit feminine heralds retained.
verses.before: The Lord gives the word; great is the company of people who proclaim it:
verses.after: The Lord gives the word; the women announcing it are a great army:
verses.tsw_comparator: The Lord gives the word; great is the company of those who proclaim it:

verses.rationale: Keep doubled flight and woman distributing spoils.
verses.before: “Kings of armies—they flee, they flee!” The women at home divide the spoil—
verses.after: “Kings of armies flee—they flee! The woman at home divides the spoil.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Kings of armies—they flee, they flee!” The women at home divide the spoil—

verses.rationale: Retain obscure sheepfold/dove scene rather than resolve roles.
verses.before: though you lie among the sheepfolds, the wings of a dove are covered with silver, and its pinions with shimmering gold.
verses.after: Though you lie among the sheepfolds, a dove’s wings are coated with silver, its pinions with shimmering gold.”
verses.tsw_comparator: though you lie among the sheepfolds, the wings of a dove are covered with silver, and its pinions with shimmering gold.

verses.rationale: Uncertain snow image and divine title retained with note.
verses.before: When the Almighty scatters kings there, it was like snow falling on Zalmon.
verses.after: When Shaddai scattered kings there, snow fell on Zalmon.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the Almighty scatters kings there, it was like snow falling on Zalmon.

verses.rationale: Literally mountain of God, preserve doubled Bashan.
verses.before: A mountain of God is the mountain of Bashan; a mountain of many peaks is the mountain of Bashan.
verses.after: A mighty mountain is Mount Bashan, a many-peaked mountain is Mount Bashan.
verses.tsw_comparator: A mountain of God is the mountain of Bashan; a mountain of many peaks is the mountain of Bashan.

verses.rationale: Personified rival peaks and chosen dwelling.
verses.before: Why do you look with envy, O mountains of many peaks, at the mountain that God desired for his dwelling— yes, where the LORD will dwell forever?
verses.after: Why look with envy, you many-peaked mountains, at the mountain God desired for his dwelling? Yes, the LORD will live there forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: Why do you look with envy, O mountains of many peaks, at the mountain that God desired for his dwelling— yes, where the LORD will dwell forever?

verses.rationale: Preserve difficult Sinai clause without inserting journey.
verses.before: The chariots of God are tens of thousands, thousands upon thousands; the Lord is among them; Sinai is now in the sanctuary.
verses.after: God’s chariots are tens of thousands, thousands upon thousands; the Lord is among them—Sinai in the sanctuary.
verses.tsw_comparator: The chariots of God are tens of thousands, thousands upon thousands; the Lord is among them; Sinai is now in the sanctuary.

verses.rationale: Received not gave; retain unsettled final relation.
verses.before: You ascended on high, leading captivity captive; you received gifts among men, even among the rebellious, that the LORD God might dwell there.
verses.after: You went up on high, leading captives away; you received gifts among people, even the rebellious, so that YAH God might dwell there.
verses.tsw_comparator: You ascended on high, leading captivity captive; you received gifts among men, even among the rebellious, that the LORD God might dwell there.

verses.rationale: Unspecified bearing object supplied as burden, noted alternative.
verses.before: Blessed be the Lord, who daily bears us up; God is our salvation.
verses.after: Blessed be the Lord, day after day; he bears our burden, the God who saves us. Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Blessed be the Lord, who daily bears us up; God is our salvation.

verses.rationale: Retain plural deliverances and both divine names.
verses.before: Our God is a God of salvation, and to God, the Lord, belong escapes from death.
verses.after: Our God is a God of rescues; to the LORD, the Lord, belong escapes from death.
verses.tsw_comparator: Our God is a God of salvation, and to God, the Lord, belong escapes from death.

verses.rationale: Preserve violent scalp detail and habitual guilt.
verses.before: Yet God will strike the head of his enemies, the hairy crown of the one who walks in his guilt.
verses.after: But God will crush his enemies’ heads, the hairy crown of one who goes on in guilt.
verses.tsw_comparator: But God will strike the head of his enemies, the hairy crown of the one who walks in his guilt.

verses.rationale: Object them inferred from enemies, repeated return retained.
verses.before: The Lord said, “I will bring them back from Bashan, I will bring them back from the depths of the sea,
verses.after: The Lord said, “I will bring them back from Bashan; I will bring them back from the depths of the sea,
verses.tsw_comparator: The Lord said, “I will bring them back from Bashan, I will bring them back from the depths of the sea,

verses.rationale: Keep pinned crush rather than wash, difficult bloody syntax noted.
verses.before: that you may strike your feet in blood, that the tongues of your dogs may have their portion from the enemies.”
verses.after: so your foot may crush them in blood and your dogs’ tongues may have their portion from enemies.”
verses.tsw_comparator: that you may strike your feet in blood, that the tongues of your dogs may have their portion from the enemies.”

verses.rationale: Repeat procession, singular personal confession within public event.
verses.before: Your procession is seen, O God, the procession of my God, my king, into the sanctuary—
verses.after: They have seen your processions, God, the processions of my God, my king, into the sanctuary.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your procession is seen, O God, the procession of my God, my king, into the sanctuary—

verses.rationale: Specific women and procession order retained.
verses.before: the singers in front, the musicians after, in the midst, young women playing tambourines.
verses.after: Singers lead, musicians follow, with young women beating tambourines between them.
verses.tsw_comparator: the singers in front, the musicians after, in the midst, young women playing tambourines.

verses.rationale: Source fountain/origin idiom clarified.
verses.before: Bless God in the congregations, the LORD, from the fountain of Israel.
verses.after: Bless God in the assemblies— the LORD, you who spring from Israel!
verses.tsw_comparator: Bless God in the congregations, the LORD, from the fountain of Israel.

verses.rationale: Four tribes and rare throng word retained.
verses.before: There is Benjamin, the youngest, leading them, the princes of Judah in their throng, the princes of Zebulun, the princes of Naphtali.
verses.after: There is little Benjamin leading them, Judah’s princes with their throng, the princes of Zebulun and the princes of Naphtali.
verses.tsw_comparator: There is Benjamin, the youngest, leading them, the princes of Judah in their throng, the princes of Zebulun, the princes of Naphtali.

verses.rationale: Pinned your God not emended command O God; voice shift retained.
verses.before: Summon your strength, O God; confirm, O God, what you have worked for us.
verses.after: Your God has commanded your strength. Show your strength, God, as you have acted for us.
verses.tsw_comparator: Summon your strength, O God; confirm, O God, what you have worked for us.

verses.rationale: Temple motive/location rather than invented procession route.
verses.before: Because of your temple at Jerusalem, kings will bring gifts to you.
verses.after: Because of your temple above Jerusalem, kings will bring you gifts.
verses.tsw_comparator: Because of your temple at Jerusalem, kings shall bring gifts to you.

verses.rationale: Difficult participle chosen active with alternate submission noted; pinned scattered retained.
verses.before: Rebuke the beast among the reeds, the herd of bulls with the calves of the peoples, trampling underfoot people who lust after tribute; scatter the peoples who delight in war.
verses.after: Rebuke the beast among the reeds, the herd of bulls among the peoples’ calves, trampling on pieces of silver. He has scattered the peoples who delight in war.
verses.tsw_comparator: Rebuke the beast among the reeds, the herd of bulls with the calves of the peoples, trampling underfoot those who lust after tribute; scatter the peoples who delight in war.

verses.rationale: Uncertain envoys noun and Cush name, no modern Ethiopia equation.
verses.before: Nobles will come from Egypt; Cush will hasten to stretch out her hands to God.
verses.after: Envoys will come from Egypt; Cush will hurry to stretch its hands to God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Nobles shall come from Egypt; Cush shall hasten to stretch out her hands to God.

verses.rationale: Keep global kingdom invitation.
verses.before: O kingdoms of the earth, sing to God; sing praises to the Lord—
verses.after: Kingdoms of the earth, sing to God; make music to the Lord. Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: O kingdoms of the earth, sing to God; sing praises to the Lord—

verses.rationale: Preserve riding and doubled heavens/voice.
verses.before: to him who rides in the ancient heavens, look, he sends out his voice, his mighty voice.
verses.after: He rides the ancient heavens, the highest heavens. Listen! He gives voice—a mighty voice.
verses.tsw_comparator: to him who rides in the ancient heavens, behold, he sends out his voice, his mighty voice.

verses.rationale: Earth people and sky paired.
verses.before: Ascribe power to God, whose majesty is over Israel, and whose power is in the skies.
verses.after: Ascribe strength to God; his majesty is over Israel, his strength in the clouds.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ascribe power to God, whose majesty is over Israel, and whose power is in the skies.

verses.rationale: Retain plural sanctuaries and closing blessing.
verses.before: Fearsome is God from his sanctuary; the God of Israel—he gives power and strength to his people. Blessed be God.
verses.after: Awesome are you, God, from your sanctuaries! The God of Israel gives strength and power to the people. Blessed be God!
verses.tsw_comparator: Fearsome is God from his sanctuary; the God of Israel—he gives power and strength to his people. Blessed be God.

verses.rationale: Nephesh bodily throat in drowning image and title preserved.
verses.before: Save me, God, for the waters have come up to my neck.
verses.after: For the music leader. According to “Lilies.” Of David. Save me, God! The waters have reached my throat.
verses.tsw_comparator: Save me, God, for the waters have come up to my neck.

verses.rationale: Keep unstable mud and engulfing water distinct.
verses.before: I have sunk in deep mire, where there is no foothold; I have come into deep waters, and the flood sweeps over me.
verses.after: I sink into deep mud with nowhere to stand. I have entered deep waters; the current sweeps me away.
verses.tsw_comparator: I have sunk in deep mire, where there is no foothold; I have come into deep waters, and the flood sweeps over me.

verses.rationale: Bodily exhaustion and waiting retained.
verses.before: I am weary with my crying; my throat is parched. My eyes fail with hoping for my God.
verses.after: I am worn out from calling; my throat is parched. My eyes fail as I wait for my God.
verses.tsw_comparator: I am weary with my crying; my throat is parched. My eyes fail with hoping for my God.

verses.rationale: Keep hair count, strong enemies and unjust restitution question.
verses.before: More than the hairs of my head are people who hate me without cause; mighty are people who would destroy me, people who attack me with lies. What I did not steal must I now restore?
verses.after: Those who hate me without cause outnumber the hairs on my head. My treacherous enemies, bent on destroying me, are powerful. Must I restore what I never stole?
verses.tsw_comparator: More than the hairs of my head are those who hate me without cause; mighty are those who would destroy me, those who attack me with lies. What I did not steal must I now restore?

verses.rationale: Confession retained alongside innocence of accusation.
verses.before: God, you know my folly, and my guilt is not hidden from you.
verses.after: God, you know my folly; my guilty deeds are not hidden from you.
verses.tsw_comparator: God, you know my folly, and my guilt is not hidden from you.

verses.rationale: Preserve repeated because of me and divine designations.
verses.before: Do not let people who hope in you be shamed because of me, O Lord God of hosts; do not let people who seek you be dishonored because of me, O God of Israel.
verses.after: Do not let those who wait for you be ashamed because of me, Lord, LORD of Armies. Do not let those who seek you be disgraced because of me, God of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not let those who hope in you be shamed because of me, O Lord God of hosts; do not let those who seek you be dishonored because of me, O God of Israel.

verses.rationale: Affliction for God not merely private conflict.
verses.before: For it is for your sake that I have borne reproach, that shame has covered my face.
verses.after: For your sake I bear reproach; disgrace covers my face.
verses.tsw_comparator: For it is for your sake that I have borne reproach, that shame has covered my face.

verses.rationale: Specific male kin retained with emphatic maternal relation.
verses.before: I have become a stranger to my brothers, a foreigner to my mother's sons.
verses.after: I have become a stranger to my brothers, an outsider to my mother’s sons.
verses.tsw_comparator: I have become a stranger to my brothers, a foreigner to my mother's sons.

verses.rationale: Preserve consuming zeal and transfer of reproaches.
verses.before: For the zeal for your house has consumed me, and the reproaches of people who reproach you have fallen on me.
verses.after: Zeal for your house has consumed me; the insults of those who insult you have fallen on me.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the zeal for your house has consumed me, and the reproaches of those who reproach you have fallen on me.

verses.rationale: Compressed weeping/fasting rendered without invented humiliation.
verses.before: When I wept and humbled my soul with fasting, it became my reproach.
verses.after: When I wept and fasted, it became another reproach against me.
verses.tsw_comparator: When I wept and humbled my soul with fasting, it became my reproach.

verses.rationale: Clothing and public ridicule.
verses.before: When I made sackcloth my clothing, I became a byword to them.
verses.after: I put on sackcloth, and I became their byword.
verses.tsw_comparator: When I made sackcloth my clothing, I became a byword to them.

verses.rationale: Retain civic gate and drinkers, no imposed social class.
verses.before: People who sit at the gate talk about me, and I am the song of drunkards.
verses.after: Those sitting at the gate talk about me; I am the song of those drinking strong drink.
verses.tsw_comparator: Those who sit at the gate talk about me, and I am the song of drunkards.

verses.rationale: Keep favorable time and truth of salvation as dependability.
verses.before: But as for me, my prayer is to you, O LORD, at an acceptable time, O God; in the abundance of your steadfast love, answer me in your saving faithfulness.
verses.after: But my prayer is to you, LORD, at a time of favor. God, in your abundant faithful love, answer me with your dependable salvation.
verses.tsw_comparator: But as for me, my prayer is to you, O LORD, at an acceptable time, O God; in the abundance of your steadfast love, answer me in your saving faithfulness.

verses.rationale: Repeat opening threat and human opponents together.
verses.before: Rescue me from the mire; do not let me sink; deliver me from my foes and from the depths of the waters.
verses.after: Pull me from the mud; do not let me sink. Let me escape those who hate me and the deep waters.
verses.tsw_comparator: Rescue me from the mire; do not let me sink; deliver me from my foes and from the depths of the waters.

verses.rationale: Three distinct swallowing dangers retained.
verses.before: Do not let the flood sweep over me, or the deep swallow me up, or the pit close its mouth over me.
verses.after: Do not let the current sweep me away, the deep swallow me, or the pit close its mouth over me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not let the flood sweep over me, or the deep swallow me up, or the pit close its mouth over me.

verses.rationale: Love and compassion both ground petition.
verses.before: Answer me, O LORD, for your steadfast love is good; according to your abundant mercy, turn to me.
verses.after: Answer me, LORD, for your faithful love is good; in your great compassion, turn toward me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Answer me, O LORD, for your steadfast love is good; according to your abundant mercy, turn to me.

verses.rationale: Urgency and hidden face retained.
verses.before: Do not hide your face from your servant; for I am in trouble, answer me quickly.
verses.after: Do not hide your face from your servant. I am in distress; hurry and answer!
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not hide your face from your servant; for I am in trouble, answer me quickly.

verses.rationale: Both redemption verbs and enemy motive.
verses.before: Draw near to my soul, redeem it; ransom me because of my enemies.
verses.after: Come near and redeem my life; because of my enemies, ransom me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Draw near to my soul, redeem it; ransom me because of my enemies.

verses.rationale: Triple humiliation and divine awareness.
verses.before: You know my reproach, my shame, and my dishonor; my adversaries are all known to you.
verses.after: You know my reproach, my shame, my disgrace; all my adversaries are before you.
verses.tsw_comparator: You know my reproach, my shame, and my dishonor; my adversaries are all known to you.

verses.rationale: Keep failed search and severe physical/emotional hurt.
verses.before: Reproach has broken my heart, and I am in despair. I looked for pity, but there was none, and for comforters, but I found none.
verses.after: Reproach has broken my heart, and I am desperately ill. I looked for sympathy—there was none; for comforters—I found no one.
verses.tsw_comparator: Reproach has broken my heart, and I am in despair. I looked for pity, but there was none, and for comforters, but I found none.

verses.rationale: Rosh poisonous/bitter substance not forced exact plant.
verses.before: They gave me poison for food, and for my thirst, they gave me vinegar to drink.
verses.after: They put poison in my food and gave me vinegar when I was thirsty.
verses.tsw_comparator: They gave me poison for food, and for my thirst, they gave me vinegar to drink.

verses.rationale: Difficult shlomim ease reading noted with recompense alternative.
verses.before: Let their table before them become a snare; when they are at peace, let it become a trap.
verses.after: Let their own table become a trap before them, a snare when they are at ease.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let their table before them become a snare; when they are at peace, let it become a trap.

verses.rationale: Preserve bodily curse rather than soften.
verses.before: Let their eyes be darkened, so they cannot see, and make their loins tremble continually.
verses.after: Let their eyes grow dark so they cannot see; make their loins tremble continually.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let their eyes be darkened, so they cannot see, and make their loins tremble continually.

verses.rationale: Two forms of divine anger retained.
verses.before: Pour out your anger upon them, and let your burning wrath overtake them.
verses.after: Pour your indignation on them; let your burning anger catch them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Pour out your anger upon them, and let your burning wrath overtake them.

verses.rationale: Plural tents retained not harmonized later quotation.
verses.before: May their camp be desolate; let none dwell in their tents.
verses.after: Let their encampment lie desolate; let no one live in their tents.
verses.tsw_comparator: May their camp be desolate; let none dwell in their tents.

verses.rationale: Divine agency and human exploitation both explicit.
verses.before: For they persecute those you have struck down, and they recount the pain of those you have wounded.
verses.after: They pursue the one you struck and recount the pain of those you wounded.
verses.tsw_comparator: For they persecute those you have struck down, and they recount the pain of those you have wounded.

verses.rationale: Keep difficult cumulative guilt and exclusion, note vindication sense.
verses.before: Add iniquity to their iniquity, and let them not come into your righteousness.
verses.after: Add wrongdoing to their wrongdoing; do not let them enter your righteousness.
verses.tsw_comparator: Add iniquity to their iniquity, and let them not come into your righteousness.

verses.rationale: Retain registration image without afterlife-system expansion.
verses.before: Let them be blotted out of the book of the living; let them not be enrolled among the righteous.
verses.after: Let them be erased from the book of the living, not enrolled with the righteous.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let them be blotted out of the book of the living; let them not be enrolled among the righteous.

verses.rationale: Contrast suffering and protective height.
verses.before: Yet I am afflicted and in pain; let your salvation, O God, set me on high.
verses.after: But I am afflicted and in pain; God, let your salvation set me high.
verses.tsw_comparator: But I am afflicted and in pain; let your salvation, O God, set me on high.

verses.rationale: Song and thankful magnification retained.
verses.before: I will praise the name of God with a song; I will magnify him with thanksgiving.
verses.after: I will praise God’s name in song and magnify him with thanksgiving.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will praise the name of God with a song; I will magnify him with thanksgiving.

verses.rationale: Keep concrete sacrificial animal traits.
verses.before: This will please the LORD more than an ox or a bull with horns and hoofs.
verses.after: This will please the LORD more than an ox, more than a bull with horns and hooves.
verses.tsw_comparator: This will please the LORD more than an ox or a bull with horns and hoofs.

verses.rationale: Shift to direct audience command retained.
verses.before: The humble will see this and be glad; you who seek God, let your hearts revive.
verses.after: The humble will see and rejoice. You who seek God, let your hearts revive!
verses.tsw_comparator: The humble shall see this and be glad; you who seek God, let your hearts revive.

verses.rationale: Prisoners his, not generalized incarceration claim.
verses.before: For the LORD hears the needy and does not despise his own people who are prisoners.
verses.after: The LORD hears the needy and does not despise his prisoners.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the LORD hears the needy and does not despise his own people who are prisoners.

verses.rationale: Nonhuman sea creatures included.
verses.before: Let heaven and earth praise him, the seas and everything that moves in them.
verses.after: Let heaven and earth praise him, the seas and everything moving in them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let heaven and earth praise him, the seas and everything that moves in them.

verses.rationale: Future community remains unspecified pronoun.
verses.before: For God will save Zion and build the cities of Judah; they will dwell there and possess it.
verses.after: God will save Zion and rebuild Judah’s towns; they will live there and possess it.
verses.tsw_comparator: For God will save Zion and build the cities of Judah; they shall dwell there and possess it.

verses.rationale: Descendants and name-love close communal scope.
verses.before: The children of his servants will inherit it, and people who love his name will dwell in it.
verses.after: His servants’ offspring will inherit it; those who love his name will dwell there.
verses.tsw_comparator: The children of his servants shall inherit it, and those who love his name shall dwell in it.

verses.rationale: Title included and compressed first clause supplied come.
verses.before: Elohim, to deliver me, LORD, to my help, hasten!
verses.after: For the music leader. Of David. For remembrance. God, come to rescue me! LORD, hurry to help me!
verses.tsw_comparator: Elohim, to deliver me, LORD, to my help, hasten!

verses.rationale: Keep two hostile groups and parallel reversal.
verses.before: Let them be put to shame and humiliated, people who seek my life. Let them turn back, and be dishonored, people who delight in my hurt.
verses.after: Let those seeking my life be ashamed and disgraced; let those who delight in my harm retreat in humiliation.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let them be put to shame and humiliated, those who seek my life. Let them turn back, and be dishonored, those who delight in my hurt.

verses.rationale: Double taunt and turning retained.
verses.before: Let them turn back because of their shame who say, "Aha! Aha!"
verses.after: Let those who say, “Aha! Aha!” turn back because of their shame.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let them turn back because of their shame who say, "Aha! Aha!"

verses.rationale: God name kept distinct from parallel Psalm 40 LORD.
verses.before: Let everyone who seek you rejoice and be glad in you. Let people who love your salvation say continually, "Great is Elohim!"
verses.after: Let all who seek you rejoice and be glad in you. Let those who love your salvation always say, “Great is God!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Let all who seek you rejoice and be glad in you. Let those who love your salvation say continually, "Great is Elohim!"

verses.rationale: Keep urgent address and both divine names.
verses.before: Yet I am poor and needy; Elohim, hasten to me. My help and my deliverer are you; LORD, do not delay.
verses.after: But I am afflicted and needy. God, hurry to me! You are my help and my rescuer; LORD, do not delay.
verses.tsw_comparator: But I am poor and needy; Elohim, hasten to me. My help and my deliverer are you; LORD, do not delay.

verses.rationale: No invented title; opening refuge retained.
verses.before: In you, O LORD, I have taken refuge; let me never be put to shame.
verses.after: In you, LORD, I take refuge; never let me be put to shame.
verses.tsw_comparator: In you, O LORD, I have taken refuge; let me never be put to shame.

verses.rationale: Two rescue verbs and listening image.
verses.before: In your righteousness, deliver me and rescue me; incline your ear to me and save me.
verses.after: In your righteousness rescue me and bring me to safety. Bend your ear toward me and save me.
verses.tsw_comparator: In your righteousness, deliver me and rescue me; incline your ear to me and save me.

verses.rationale: Pinned dwelling and commanded, not harmonized Psalm31.
verses.before: Be to me a rock of refuge, to which I may continually come; you have given the command to save me, for you are my rock and my fortress.
verses.after: Be my rock, a dwelling I can always enter. You have commanded my rescue, for you are my crag and my fortress.
verses.tsw_comparator: Be to me a rock of refuge, to which I may continually come; you have given the command to save me, for you are my rock and my fortress.

verses.rationale: Keep hands and violence, difficult ruthless term.
verses.before: Deliver me, my God, from the hand of the wicked, from the grasp of the unjust and cruel.
verses.after: My God, free me from the wicked man’s hand, from the grip of the unjust and ruthless.
verses.tsw_comparator: Deliver me, my God, from the hand of the wicked, from the grasp of the unjust and cruel.

verses.rationale: Both divine names retained without collapsing title.
verses.before: For you are my hope, O Lord GOD, my trust from my youth.
verses.after: You are my hope, Lord, LORD, my trust since youth.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you are my hope, O Lord GOD, my trust from my youth.

verses.rationale: Gozi birth assistance rendering with uncertainty noted.
verses.before: Upon you I have relied from my birth; it was you who took me from my mother's womb. My praise is continually of you.
verses.after: I have leaned on you since birth; you brought me out of my mother’s womb. My praise is always of you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Upon you I have relied from my birth; it was you who took me from my mother's womb. My praise is continually of you.

verses.rationale: Portent may be ominous, not automatically positive example.
verses.before: I have been a wonder to many, but you are my strong refuge.
verses.after: I have become a sign to many, but you are my strong refuge.
verses.tsw_comparator: I have been a wonder to many, but you are my strong refuge.

verses.rationale: Mouth filled with sustained praise.
verses.before: My mouth is filled with your praise, and with your glory all day.
verses.after: Let my mouth be filled with your praise, with your splendor all day long.
verses.tsw_comparator: My mouth is filled with your praise, and with your glory all day.

verses.rationale: Aging and diminished strength explicit.
verses.before: Do not cast me off in the time of old age; do not forsake me when my strength fails.
verses.after: Do not cast me aside in old age; do not forsake me when my strength is spent.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not cast me off in the time of old age; do not forsake me when my strength fails.

verses.rationale: Keep vigilance as threat to life.
verses.before: For my enemies speak against me, people who watch for my life consult together,
verses.after: My enemies speak against me; those watching for my life take counsel together,
verses.tsw_comparator: For my enemies speak against me, those who watch for my life consult together,

verses.rationale: Quote enemy claim, not narrator endorsement.
verses.before: saying, "God has forsaken him, pursue and seize him, for there is none to deliver."
verses.after: saying, “God has forsaken him. Pursue him and seize him; no one will rescue him.”
verses.tsw_comparator: saying, "God has forsaken him, pursue and seize him, for there is none to deliver."

verses.rationale: Follow read hurry; repeated God retained.
verses.before: O God, do not be far from me; my God, hasten to help me.
verses.after: God, do not stay far from me; my God, hurry to help me!
verses.tsw_comparator: O God, do not be far from me; my God, hasten to help me.

verses.rationale: Keep consumed and clothing humiliation.
verses.before: Let people who are adversaries of my soul be ashamed and consumed; let them be covered with reproach and dishonor, who seek my hurt.
verses.after: Let my accusers be ashamed and consumed; let those seeking my harm wrap themselves in reproach and disgrace.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let those who are adversaries of my soul be ashamed and consumed; let them be covered with reproach and dishonor, who seek my hurt.

verses.rationale: Continued hope and increasing praise.
verses.before: Yet I will hope continually, and will praise you more and more.
verses.after: But I will keep hoping and add still more to all your praise.
verses.tsw_comparator: But I will hope continually, and will praise you more and more.

verses.rationale: Rare counts word rendered counting not literary knowledge.
verses.before: My mouth will tell of your righteousness, of your salvation all day long, though I know not their numbers.
verses.after: My mouth will recount your righteousness, your salvation all day long, though I cannot count its deeds.
verses.tsw_comparator: My mouth will tell of your righteousness, of your salvation all day long, though I know not their numbers.

verses.rationale: Retain coming with deeds and exclusive praise.
verses.before: I will come in the strength of the Lord GOD; I will make mention of your righteousness, yours alone.
verses.after: I will come with the mighty deeds of the Lord, the LORD; I will tell of your righteousness, yours alone.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will come in the strength of the Lord GOD; I will make mention of your righteousness, yours alone.

verses.rationale: Lifelong teaching and testimony.
verses.before: O God, you have taught me from my youth, and I still declare your wondrous deeds.
verses.after: God, you have taught me since youth; until now I have told of your wonders.
verses.tsw_comparator: O God, you have taught me from my youth, and I still declare your wondrous deeds.

verses.rationale: Preserve arm and transmission across generations.
verses.before: Even to old age and gray hairs, O God, do not forsake me, until I declare your power to the next generation, your might to everyone who are to come.
verses.after: Even when I am old and gray, God, do not forsake me, until I tell the next generation of your arm, and all who are to come of your might.
verses.tsw_comparator: Even to old age and gray hairs, O God, do not forsake me, until I declare your power to the next generation, your might to all who are to come.

verses.rationale: Repeated God and incomparable deeds.
verses.before: Your righteousness, O God, reaches to the high heavens, you who have done great things. O God, who is like you?
verses.after: Your righteousness, God, reaches the heights. You have done great things; God, who is like you?
verses.tsw_comparator: Your righteousness, O God, reaches to the high heavens, you who have done great things. O God, who is like you?

verses.rationale: Read me in two variants rather than written us; repeated again.
verses.before: You who have shown me many troubles and evils, you will restore my life again; from the depths of the earth you will bring me up again.
verses.after: You have made me see many bitter troubles; you will revive me again, bring me up again from the earth’s depths.
verses.tsw_comparator: You who have shown me many troubles and evils, you will restore my life again; from the depths of the earth you will bring me up again.

verses.rationale: Petition chosen from imperfect forms, comfort not prosperity gloss.
verses.before: You will increase my greatness and comfort me once more.
verses.after: Increase my honor; turn and comfort me.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will increase my greatness and comfort me once more.

verses.rationale: Distinct instruments and divine title.
verses.before: I will also praise you with the harp for your faithfulness, O my God; I will sing praises to you with the lyre, O Holy One of Israel.
verses.after: I too will thank you with the harp for your faithfulness, my God; I will make music to you with the lyre, Holy One of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will also praise you with the harp for your faithfulness, O my God; I will sing praises to you with the lyre, O Holy One of Israel.

verses.rationale: Mouth and whole living self praise together.
verses.before: My lips will shout for joy when I sing praises to you, my soul, which you have redeemed.
verses.after: My lips will shout for joy when I make music to you, and so will my life, which you redeemed.
verses.tsw_comparator: My lips will shout for joy when I sing praises to you, my soul, which you have redeemed.

verses.rationale: Turn from threatened future to confidence in shame.
verses.before: My tongue will declare your righteousness all day long, for they have been put to shame, for they have been humiliated, people who seek to harm me.
verses.after: My tongue will ponder your righteousness all day, for those seeking my harm are ashamed and disgraced.
verses.tsw_comparator: My tongue will declare your righteousness all day long, for they have been put to shame, for they have been humiliated, those who seek to harm me.

verses.rationale: Title of/for Solomon ambiguity noted; justice royal gift.
verses.before: For Solomon. O God, give the king your judgments, and your righteousness to the king's son.
verses.after: Of Solomon. God, give the king your judgments, the king’s son your righteousness.
verses.tsw_comparator: For Solomon. O God, give the king your judgments, and your righteousness to the king's son.

verses.rationale: Royal petition not guaranteed history.
verses.before: May he judge your people with righteousness and your poor with justice.
verses.after: May he judge your people with righteousness and your afflicted ones with justice.
verses.tsw_comparator: May he judge your people with righteousness and your poor with justice.

verses.rationale: Keep geographical personification and righteousness as the means of peace.
verses.before: Let the mountains bring peace to the people, and the hills, by righteousness.
verses.after: May the mountains bring peace to the people, and the hills bring it through righteousness.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let the mountains bring peace to the people, and the hills, by righteousness.

verses.rationale: Children and violent crushing not generalized benevolence.
verses.before: May he judge the poor of the people, save the children of the needy, and crush the oppressor.
verses.after: May he defend the afflicted among the people, save the children of the needy, and crush the oppressor.
verses.tsw_comparator: May he judge the poor of the people, save the children of the needy, and crush the oppressor.

verses.rationale: Pinned they fear you not emended king lives; referent note.
verses.before: May they fear you while the sun endures, and as long as the moon, through all generations.
verses.after: May they revere you while the sun endures, as long as the moon, generation after generation.
verses.tsw_comparator: May they fear you while the sun endures, and as long as the moon, through all generations.

verses.rationale: Gez cut grass with fleece alternative, preserve descent.
verses.before: May he come down like rain upon the mown grass, like showers that water the earth.
verses.after: May he come down like rain on cut grass, like showers watering the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: May he come down like rain upon the mown grass, like showers that water the earth.

verses.rationale: Cosmic duration and righteous persons retained.
verses.before: In his days may the righteous flourish, and abundance of peace, till the moon is no more.
verses.after: In his days may the righteous flourish and peace abound until the moon is no more.
verses.tsw_comparator: In his days may the righteous flourish, and abundance of peace, till the moon is no more.

verses.rationale: River capitalized with Euphrates note, no inserted geography.
verses.before: May he rule from sea to sea, and from the River to the ends of the earth.
verses.after: May he rule from sea to sea, from the River to earth’s ends.
verses.tsw_comparator: May he rule from sea to sea, and from the River to the ends of the earth.

verses.rationale: Keep submission and degrading dust image.
verses.before: Before him let desert tribes bow, and his enemies lick the dust.
verses.after: May desert dwellers bow before him and his enemies lick the dust.
verses.tsw_comparator: Before him let desert tribes bow, and his enemies lick the dust.

verses.rationale: Sheba/Seba not collapsed.
verses.before: May the kings of Tarshish and of the islands bring tribute; the kings of Sheba and Seba offer gifts.
verses.after: May the kings of Tarshish and the coastlands bring tribute, the kings of Sheba and Seba offer gifts.
verses.tsw_comparator: May the kings of Tarshish and of the islands bring tribute; the kings of Sheba and Seba offer gifts.

verses.rationale: Royal worldwide submission retained.
verses.before: Let all kings bow down to him, all nations serve him.
verses.after: May all kings bow before him, all nations serve him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let all kings bow down to him, all nations serve him.

verses.rationale: Reason for reign is rescue of vulnerable.
verses.before: For he will deliver the needy who cry out, the poor and him who has no helper.
verses.after: For he rescues the needy who cry out, the afflicted who have no helper.
verses.tsw_comparator: For he will deliver the needy who cry out, the poor and him who has no helper.

verses.rationale: Repeated needy preserved.
verses.before: He will have compassion on the poor and needy, and the lives of the needy he will save.
verses.after: He has pity on the weak and needy and saves the lives of the needy.
verses.tsw_comparator: He will have compassion on the poor and needy, and the lives of the needy he will save.

verses.rationale: Blood value image not abstract dignity replacement.
verses.before: He will redeem their life from oppression and violence, and their blood will be precious in his sight.
verses.after: He redeems their lives from oppression and violence; their blood is precious in his eyes.
verses.tsw_comparator: He will redeem their life from oppression and violence, and their blood will be precious in his sight.

verses.rationale: Ambiguous pronouns retained, passive supplies no named donor.
verses.before: Long may he live! May gold from Sheba be given to him. May people pray for him continually and bless him all day long.
verses.after: May he live, and may gold from Sheba be given to him. May prayer be made for him continually, and blessing offered to him all day.
verses.tsw_comparator: Long may he live! May gold from Sheba be given to him. May people pray for him continually and bless him all day long.

verses.rationale: Rare abundance word and luxuriant city image retained.
verses.before: May there be abundance of grain in the land, on the tops of the mountains. May its fruit wave like Lebanon, and may people flourish in the cities like the grass of the earth.
verses.after: May grain abound in the land, even on the mountain tops; may its fruit wave like Lebanon, and people bloom from the city like the earth’s grass.
verses.tsw_comparator: May there be abundance of grain in the land, on the tops of the mountains. May its fruit wave like Lebanon, and may people flourish in the cities like the grass of the earth.

verses.rationale: Read flourish; reflexive blessing not automatically passive blessed.
verses.before: May his name endure forever, may his name increase as long as the sun shines. May nations be blessed in him; may they bless him.
verses.after: May his name last forever, may his name flourish as long as the sun. May all nations bless themselves by him and call him happy.
verses.tsw_comparator: May his name endure forever, may his name increase as long as the sun shines. May nations be blessed in him; may they bless him.

verses.rationale: Doxology distinguished from royal address.
verses.before: Blessed be the LORD God, the God of Israel, who alone does wondrous things.
verses.after: Blessed be the LORD God, the God of Israel, who alone does wonders.
verses.tsw_comparator: Blessed be the LORD God, the God of Israel, who alone does wondrous things.

verses.rationale: Double amen and universal glory preserved.
verses.before: And blessed be his glorious name forever; may the entire earth be filled with his glory. Amen and Amen.
verses.after: Blessed be his glorious name forever; may his glory fill the whole earth. Amen and amen.
verses.tsw_comparator: And blessed be his glorious name forever; may the whole earth be filled with his glory. Amen and Amen.

verses.rationale: Collection colophon retained despite further David titles later.
verses.before: The prayers of David, the son of Jesse, are ended.
verses.after: The prayers of David son of Jesse are ended.
verses.tsw_comparator: The prayers of David, the son of Jesse, are ended.

verses.rationale: Retains Israel and the heart qualification rather than emending to the upright.
verses.before: A psalm of Asaph. Truly God is good to Israel, to people who are pure in heart.
verses.after: A psalm of Asaph. God is indeed good to Israel, to those whose hearts are pure.
verses.tsw_comparator: A psalm of Asaph. Truly God is good to Israel, to those who are pure in heart.

verses.rationale: Reads both qere verbs as the poet's threatened fall.
verses.before: But as for me, my feet had almost stumbled; my steps had nearly slipped.
verses.after: But as for me, my feet had nearly slipped; I almost lost my footing.
verses.tsw_comparator: But as for me, my feet had almost stumbled; my steps had nearly slipped.

verses.rationale: Connects envy to the wicked's shalom, their apparent well-being.
verses.before: For I was envious of the boastful when I saw the prosperity of the wicked.
verses.after: I envied the arrogant when I saw how well the wicked lived.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I was envious of the boastful when I saw the prosperity of the wicked.

verses.rationale: Retains the written reference to their death; flags the difficult claim in a note.
verses.before: For they have no distress in their death; their bodies are healthy.
verses.after: They suffer no pangs at death; their bodies are well fed.
verses.tsw_comparator: For they have no distress in their death; their bodies are healthy.

verses.rationale: Keeps the speaker's sweeping perception rather than softening it into sometimes.
verses.before: They are not in trouble as other humans are; they are not stricken like the rest of humankind.
verses.after: They escape the hardships other people bear; they are not struck down like everyone else.
verses.tsw_comparator: They are not in trouble as other humans are; they are not stricken like the rest of humankind.

verses.rationale: Preserves both wearable images and explicit violence.
verses.before: So pride is their necklace, and violence clothes them as a garment.
verses.after: So pride hangs around their necks like a necklace, and violence wraps them like a garment.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore pride is their necklace, and violence clothes them as a garment.

verses.rationale: Keeps the bodily image instead of replacing eyes with iniquity.
verses.before: Their eyes bulge with fatness; the imaginations of their hearts run wild.
verses.after: Their eyes bulge from fatness; the imaginings of their hearts spill over.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their eyes bulge with fatness; the imaginations of their hearts run wild.

verses.rationale: Makes the relation of evil speech and oppression readable.
verses.before: They mock and speak with malice; they speak arrogantly of oppression.
verses.after: They sneer and speak maliciously; from their lofty place they threaten oppression.
verses.tsw_comparator: They mock and speak with malice; they speak arrogantly of oppression.

verses.rationale: Retains the extravagant mouth and roaming tongue imagery.
verses.before: They set their mouths against the heavens, and their tongues strut through the earth.
verses.after: They set their mouths against heaven, and their tongues roam the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set their mouths against the heavens, and their tongues strut through the earth.

verses.rationale: Follows the qere turn; leaves his referent unsettled and notes the obscure water image.
verses.before: So his people turn back to them and find no fault in them.
verses.after: So his people turn toward them and drink their water to the full.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore his people turn back to them and find no fault in them.

verses.rationale: Preserves the two questions and divine title.
verses.before: And they say, "How does God know? Is there knowledge in the Most High?"
verses.after: They say, “How could God know? Does the Most High know anything?”
verses.tsw_comparator: And they say, "How does God know? Is there knowledge in the Most High?"

verses.rationale: Keeps the poet's accusing observation and accumulation.
verses.before: Look, these are the wicked—always at ease, they increase in riches.
verses.after: Look at them—the wicked! Always at ease, they pile up wealth.
verses.tsw_comparator: Behold, these are the wicked—always at ease, they increase in riches.

verses.rationale: Makes the disillusionment explicit without treating it as the psalm's final claim.
verses.before: Surely in vain I have kept my heart pure and washed my hands in innocence.
verses.after: Surely I have kept my heart pure for nothing and washed my hands in innocence in vain.
verses.tsw_comparator: Surely in vain I have kept my heart pure and washed my hands in innocence.

verses.rationale: Retains the daily and morning repetition of affliction.
verses.before: For all day long I have been plagued and rebuked every morning.
verses.after: All day long I am struck down; every morning brings correction.
verses.tsw_comparator: For all day long I have been plagued and rebuked every morning.

verses.rationale: Keeps the turn to God and the communal consequence of speaking.
verses.before: If I had said, "I will speak thus," I would have betrayed the generation of your children.
verses.after: If I had said, “I will speak that way,” I would have betrayed the family of your children.
verses.tsw_comparator: If I had said, "I will speak thus," I would have betrayed the generation of your children.

verses.rationale: Preserves the unfinished movement into the sanctuary verse.
verses.before: But when I thought how to understand this, it seemed to me a wearisome task,
verses.after: I tried to understand all this, but it was too painful for me—
verses.tsw_comparator: But when I thought how to understand this, it seemed to me a wearisome task,

verses.rationale: Retains plural sanctuaries and interprets their end without adding an afterlife scheme.
verses.before: until I went into the sanctuary of God; then I discerned their end.
verses.after: until I entered God's sanctuaries and understood where their lives were heading.
verses.tsw_comparator: until I went into the sanctuary of God; then I discerned their end.

verses.rationale: Connects their slippery position with the poet's near slip in verse 2.
verses.before: Truly, you set them in slippery places; you make them fall to ruin.
verses.after: Yes, you set them on slippery ground; you bring them crashing into ruin.
verses.tsw_comparator: Truly, you set them in slippery places; you make them fall to ruin.

verses.rationale: Retains abruptness and both destruction clauses.
verses.before: How they are destroyed in a moment, swept away utterly by terrors!
verses.after: How suddenly they are devastated! Terrors sweep them away and finish them.
verses.tsw_comparator: How they are destroyed in a moment, swept away utterly by terrors!

verses.rationale: Retains the dream and image analogy; notes the difficult when-you-rise expression.
verses.before: Like a dream when one awakes, Lord, when you rouse yourself, you despise their images.
verses.after: Like a dream when someone wakes, Lord, when you rise, you dismiss their image.
verses.tsw_comparator: Like a dream when one awakes, Lord, when you rouse yourself, you despise their images.

verses.rationale: Renders kidneys as the inner seat of pain, retaining the piercing action.
verses.before: When my heart was grieved, and I was pierced within,
verses.after: When my heart turned bitter and pain pierced me deep inside,
verses.tsw_comparator: When my heart was grieved, and I was pierced within,

verses.rationale: Keeps the poet's self-description rather than labeling other people beasts.
verses.before: I was senseless and ignorant; I was like a beast before you.
verses.after: I was senseless and uncomprehending— like an animal before you.
verses.tsw_comparator: I was senseless and ignorant; I was like a beast before you.

verses.rationale: Retains the emphatic continuing relationship and specified right hand.
verses.before: Even so, I am continually with you; you hold me by my right hand.
verses.after: Yet I am always with you; you hold my right hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: Nevertheless, I am continually with you; you hold me by my right hand.

verses.rationale: Preserves receive and honor/glory without making the destination explicit.
verses.before: You guide me with your counsel, and afterward you take me to glory.
verses.after: You guide me with your counsel, and afterward you will receive me with honor.
verses.tsw_comparator: You guide me with your counsel, and afterward you take me to glory.

verses.rationale: Retains paired heaven and earth and personal desire.
verses.before: Whom have I in heaven but you? And there is nothing on earth that I desire besides you.
verses.after: Who do I have in heaven but you? With you, I desire nothing on earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whom have I in heaven but you? And there is nothing on earth that I desire besides you.

verses.rationale: Keeps rock and portion as distinct images amid bodily failure.
verses.before: My flesh and my heart may fail, but God is the strength of my heart and my portion forever.
verses.after: My body and my heart may fail, but God is my heart's rock and my portion forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: My flesh and my heart may fail, but God is the strength of my heart and my portion forever.

verses.rationale: Renders the sexual infidelity metaphor as covenantal unfaithfulness, noted explicitly.
verses.before: Indeed, people who are far from you will perish; you destroy everyone who are unfaithful to you.
verses.after: Those far from you will perish; you put an end to everyone who is unfaithful to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Indeed, those who are far from you will perish; you destroy all who are unfaithful to you.

verses.rationale: Retains both divine designations and the final turn from his refuge to your works.
verses.before: But as for me, it is good to be near God; I have made the Lord GOD my refuge, that I may tell of all your works.
verses.after: But for me, being near God is good. I have made the Lord, the LORD, my refuge, so I can tell of all your works.
verses.tsw_comparator: But as for me, it is good to be near God; I have made the Lord GOD my refuge, that I may tell of all your works.

verses.rationale: Keeps the maskil label, forever protest, smoke and flock images.
verses.before: Why, O God, have you rejected us forever? Why does your anger smoke against the sheep of your pasture?
verses.after: A maskil of Asaph. God, why have you rejected us forever? Why does your anger smoke against the sheep of your pasture?
verses.tsw_comparator: Why, O God, have you rejected us forever? Why does your anger smoke against the sheep of your pasture?

verses.rationale: Preserves acquisition, redemption and inheritance relationships.
verses.before: Remember your congregation, which you have purchased from of old, the tribe of your inheritance, which you have redeemed— Mount Zion, where you have dwelt.
verses.after: Remember the community you acquired long ago, the tribe you redeemed as your own possession— Mount Zion, where you made your home.
verses.tsw_comparator: Remember your congregation, which you have purchased from of old, the tribe of your inheritance, which you have redeemed— Mount Zion, where you have dwelt.

verses.rationale: Turns lift your steps into a natural invitation while keeping enduring devastation.
verses.before: Turn your steps toward these perpetual ruins; the enemy has damaged everything in the sanctuary.
verses.after: Walk among these lasting ruins; see all the damage the enemy has done in the sanctuary.
verses.tsw_comparator: Turn your steps toward these perpetual ruins; the enemy has damaged everything in the sanctuary.

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated signs with a modest contextual clarification.
verses.before: Your adversaries have roared among your meeting place; they have set up their own signs for signs.
verses.after: Your enemies roared inside your meeting place; they set up their own signs as signs of victory.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your adversaries have roared in the midst of your meeting place; they have set up their own signs for signs.

verses.rationale: Retains the difficult visual comparison rather than inventing a named army.
verses.before: It is known as if someone raises axes against a thicket of trees.
verses.after: They looked like people swinging axes through a thicket of trees.
verses.tsw_comparator: It is known as if someone raises axes against a thicket of trees.

verses.rationale: Follows the qere now and preserves both destructive tools.
verses.before: And now they carve all its carved work, all at once, with hatchet and hammers.
verses.after: And now they smash all its carved woodwork with hatchets and hammers.
verses.tsw_comparator: And now they carve all its carved work, all at once, with hatchet and hammers.

verses.rationale: Keeps fire, desecration and the name's dwelling together.
verses.before: They have set fire to your sanctuary; they have defiled the dwelling place of your name to the ground.
verses.after: They set your sanctuary on fire; they defiled the dwelling of your name, leveling it to the ground.
verses.tsw_comparator: They have set fire to your sanctuary; they have defiled the dwelling place of your name to the ground.

verses.rationale: Retains the obscure resolve to oppress and avoids anachronistic synagogues.
verses.before: They said in their hearts, “Let us oppress them altogether”; they have burned all the meeting places of God in the land.
verses.after: They said in their hearts, “We will crush them all.” They burned every meeting place of God in the land.
verses.tsw_comparator: They said in their hearts, “Let us oppress them altogether”; they have burned all the meeting places of God in the land.

verses.rationale: Preserves signs in contrast to enemy signs and the unanswered duration.
verses.before: We do not see our signs; there is no longer any prophet among us, and none of us knows how long.
verses.after: We see none of our signs. There is no prophet left, and no one among us knows how long this will last.
verses.tsw_comparator: We do not see our signs; there is no longer any prophet among us, and none of us knows how long.

verses.rationale: Keeps both duration questions addressed to God.
verses.before: How long, O God, will the adversary taunt? Will the enemy revile your name forever?
verses.after: God, how long will the foe mock you? Will the enemy scorn your name forever?
verses.tsw_comparator: How long, O God, shall the adversary taunt? Will the enemy revile your name forever?

verses.rationale: Preserves the demanding imperative and right-hand body image.
verses.before: Why do you hold back your hand, even your right hand? Take it from your bosom and destroy them!
verses.after: Why do you hold back your hand, your right hand? Pull it from the fold of your robe and finish them!
verses.tsw_comparator: Why do you hold back your hand, even your right hand? Take it from your bosom and destroy them!

verses.rationale: Keeps the singular my within the communal prayer and plural rescues.
verses.before: Yet God is my King from of old, working salvation among the earth.
verses.after: Yet God has been my king from long ago, working acts of rescue throughout the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet God is my King from of old, working salvation in the midst of the earth.

verses.rationale: Retains sea monsters and plural heads without reducing them to historical armies.
verses.before: You split open the sea by your strength; you broke the heads of the sea monsters in the waters.
verses.after: You broke the sea apart by your strength; you shattered the heads of the sea monsters on the waters.
verses.tsw_comparator: You split open the sea by your strength; you broke the heads of the sea monsters in the waters.

verses.rationale: Retains multiheaded Leviathan; notes the uncertain desert recipients.
verses.before: You crushed the heads of Leviathan; you gave him as food for the creatures of the wilderness.
verses.after: You crushed Leviathan's heads and gave him as food to creatures of the desert.
verses.tsw_comparator: You crushed the heads of Leviathan; you gave him as food for the creatures of the wilderness.
