verses.rationale: Keeps paired provision and drying of enduring rivers.
verses.before: You opened the springs and torrents; you dried up mighty rivers.
verses.after: You split open springs and streams; you dried up rivers that never ran dry.
verses.tsw_comparator: You opened the springs and torrents; you dried up mighty rivers.

verses.rationale: Retains the less specific light rather than silently replacing it with moon.
verses.before: Yours is the day, yours also the night; you have established light and the sun.
verses.after: The day is yours, and so is the night; you established the light and the sun.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yours is the day, yours also the night; you have established light and the sun.

verses.rationale: Keeps space and seasons as paired creation acts.
verses.before: You set all the boundaries of the earth; you made summer and winter.
verses.after: You set all the earth's boundaries; you formed summer and winter.
verses.tsw_comparator: You set all the boundaries of the earth; you made summer and winter.

verses.rationale: Retains remember and specific name address without identifying an unstated nation.
verses.before: Remember this: the enemy has mocked, O LORD, and a foolish people have reviled your name.
verses.after: Remember this, LORD: the enemy has mocked you; a foolish people has treated your name with contempt.
verses.tsw_comparator: Remember this: the enemy has mocked, O LORD, and a foolish people have reviled your name.

verses.rationale: Retains dove vulnerability and the repeated life language.
verses.before: Do not give the life of your dove to the wild beasts; do not forget the life of your afflicted forever.
verses.after: Do not hand the life of your dove over to wild beasts; do not forget the lives of your afflicted people forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not give the life of your dove to the wild beasts; do not forget the life of your afflicted forever.

verses.rationale: Keeps covenant as the appeal's ground and violence in hidden places.
verses.before: Look to the covenant, for the dark places of the earth are full of violence.
verses.after: Look to your covenant, for the land's dark places are full of dens of violence.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look to the covenant, for the dark places of the earth are full of violence.

verses.rationale: Retains both negative petition and desired praise.
verses.before: Do not let the crushed be turned away in shame; let the poor and needy praise your name.
verses.after: Do not let the crushed turn back in shame; let the poor and needy praise your name.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not let the crushed be turned away in shame; let the poor and needy praise your name.

verses.rationale: Keeps legal contest and the all-day insult directed at God.
verses.before: Arise, O God, defend your cause; remember how the foolish reproach you all day.
verses.after: Rise, God, and plead your own cause! Remember how fools mock you all day long.
verses.tsw_comparator: Arise, O God, defend your cause; remember how the foolish reproach you all day.

verses.rationale: Maintains the final unresolved demand and rising noise.
verses.before: Do not forget the voice of your adversaries, the clamor of those rising against you, which ascends continually.
verses.after: Do not forget the voices of your enemies, the uproar of those who rise against you, always growing louder.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not forget the voice of your adversaries, the clamor of those rising against you, which ascends continually.

verses.rationale: Retains all title elements, doubled thanks and the near name.
verses.before: We give thanks to you, O God; we give thanks, for your name is near. People declare your wondrous works.
verses.after: For the music leader. “Do Not Destroy.” A psalm of Asaph. A song. We thank you, God; we thank you. Your name is near; people tell of your wonders.
verses.tsw_comparator: We give thanks to you, O God; we give thanks, for your name is near. People declare your wondrous works.

verses.rationale: Marks the new divine voice without inserting a source-absent speech formula.
verses.before: “When I select the appointed time, I will judge with fairness.
verses.after: “When I choose the appointed time, I will judge fairly.
verses.tsw_comparator: “When I select the appointed time, I will judge with fairness.

verses.rationale: Keeps the earth's pillars and divine first-person contrast.
verses.before: The earth and all its inhabitants dissolve, but I uphold its pillars. Selah
verses.after: When the earth and everyone in it give way, I am the one who holds its pillars firm. Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: The earth and all its inhabitants dissolve, but I uphold its pillars. Selah

verses.rationale: Retains horn as a linked power image rather than varying it away.
verses.before: I say to the boastful, ‘Do not boast,’ and to the wicked, ‘Do not lift up the horn.
verses.after: I say to the boastful, ‘Do not boast,’ and to the wicked, ‘Do not lift your horn.
verses.tsw_comparator: I say to the boastful, ‘Do not boast,’ and to the wicked, ‘Do not lift up the horn.

verses.rationale: Preserves both horn and neck images, closing the divine warning.
verses.before: Do not lift up your horn on high, do not speak with insolent neck.’”
verses.after: Do not lift your horn on high or speak with your neck stiff in arrogance.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not lift up your horn on high, do not speak with insolent neck.’”

verses.rationale: Reads harim as lifting up in the contextual wordplay; notes the mountain alternative.
verses.before: For neither from the east nor from the west, nor from the wilderness comes exaltation.
verses.after: For exaltation comes neither from the east nor from the west, nor from the wilderness.
verses.tsw_comparator: For neither from the east nor from the west, nor from the wilderness comes exaltation.

verses.rationale: Keeps lowering and raising as the explanation of exaltation.
verses.before: Yet God is the judge; he puts down one and exalts another.
verses.after: God is the judge: he brings one down and raises another up.
verses.tsw_comparator: But God is the judge; he puts down one and exalts another.

verses.rationale: Retains cup, mixed wine and compulsory drinking of residue.
verses.before: For a cup is in the hand of the Lord, full of foaming wine mixed with spices, and he pours out from it. But its dregs, all the wicked of the earth will drink, draining it to the last drop.
verses.after: The LORD holds a cup in his hand, full of foaming wine mixed with spices. He pours it out, and all the earth's wicked must drain it, down to the dregs.
verses.tsw_comparator: For a cup is in the hand of the Lord, full of foaming wine mixed with spices, and he pours out from it. But its dregs, all the wicked of the earth will drink, draining it to the last drop.

verses.rationale: Keeps the speaker's first-person declaration distinct from judgment speech.
verses.before: Yet I will declare forever; I will sing praises to the God of Jacob.
verses.after: But I will tell of this forever; I will sing to the God of Jacob.
verses.tsw_comparator: But I will declare forever; I will sing praises to the God of Jacob.

verses.rationale: Preserves the resumed first-person claim; notes speaker uncertainty rather than settling it silently.
verses.before: All the horns of the wicked I will cut off, but the horns of the righteous will be exalted.
verses.after: “I will cut off every horn of the wicked, but the horns of the righteous will be lifted high.”
verses.tsw_comparator: All the horns of the wicked I will cut off, but the horns of the righteous will be exalted.

verses.rationale: Retains musical instruction and Judah/Israel pairing.
verses.before: God is known in Judah; God’s name is great in Israel.
verses.after: For the music leader. With stringed instruments. A psalm of Asaph. A song. God is known in Judah; his name is great in Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: God is known in Judah; God’s name is great in Israel.

verses.rationale: Keeps Salem as a place name and shelter distinct from dwelling.
verses.before: The shelter of God is in Salem, and the dwelling place in Zion.
verses.after: His shelter is in Salem; his dwelling is in Zion.
verses.tsw_comparator: The shelter of God is in Salem, and the dwelling place in Zion.

verses.rationale: Retains fiery shafts and the full weapon list.
verses.before: There God broke the flaming arrows, the shield, the sword, and the weapons of war. Selah.
verses.after: There he shattered the bow's fiery arrows, the shield, the sword, the weapons of war. Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: There God broke the flaming arrows, the shield, the sword, and the weapons of war. Selah.

verses.rationale: Preserves the pinned mountains of prey rather than emending to everlasting mountains.
verses.before: You are radiant, majestic, from the mountains of prey.
verses.after: You shine with light, more majestic than mountains rich with prey.
verses.tsw_comparator: You are radiant, majestic, from the mountains of prey.

verses.rationale: Keeps plundering, sleep and disabled hands without euphemizing defeat.
verses.before: The stouthearted were plundered; they sank into their sleep. None of the warriors could find their hands.
verses.after: The stouthearted have been stripped bare; they have sunk into sleep. None of the warriors can lift a hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: The stouthearted were plundered; they sank into their sleep. None of the warriors could find their hands.

verses.rationale: Retains chariot rather than substituting rider and preserves the sleep image.
verses.before: At your rebuke, O God of Jacob, both chariot and horse lay stunned.
verses.after: At your rebuke, God of Jacob, chariot and horse lie in deep sleep.
verses.tsw_comparator: At your rebuke, O God of Jacob, both chariot and horse lay stunned.

verses.rationale: Keeps emphatic doubled you and fearful question.
verses.before: You—you are to be feared. Who can stand before you when your anger rises?
verses.after: You—you are to be feared! Who can stand before you once your anger rises?
verses.tsw_comparator: You—you are to be feared. Who can stand before you when your anger rises?

verses.rationale: Keeps silence as response to the heavenly verdict and continues the sentence.
verses.before: From the heavens you caused judgment to be heard; the earth feared and was still
verses.after: You announced judgment from heaven; the earth grew afraid and fell silent
verses.tsw_comparator: From the heavens you caused judgment to be heard; the earth feared and was still

verses.rationale: Retains the rescue purpose and worldwide afflicted.
verses.before: when God rose up for judgment, to save all the humble of the earth. Selah.
verses.after: when God rose to judge, to save all the afflicted of the earth. Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: when God rose up for judgment, to save all the humble of the earth. Selah.

verses.rationale: Retains the difficult girding image; notes alternative restraint reading.
verses.before: Surely human wrath will praise you; the remnant of wrath you bind around you.
verses.after: Even human rage will praise you; you wrap yourself in the rage that remains.
verses.tsw_comparator: Surely human wrath will praise you; the remnant of wrath you bind around you.

verses.rationale: Preserves fulfillment and the fearful title rather than weakening it to respect.
verses.before: Make vows to the LORD your God and fulfill them; let everyone who are around God bring gifts to the One who is to be feared.
verses.after: Make vows to the LORD your God and fulfill them; let everyone around him bring gifts to the One to be feared.
verses.tsw_comparator: Make vows to the LORD your God and fulfill them; let all who are around God bring gifts to the One who is to be feared.

verses.rationale: Keeps spirit/breath ambiguity and the final political scope.
verses.before: God cuts off the spirit of princes and is fearsome to the kings of the earth.
verses.after: He cuts off the spirit of rulers; he fills the kings of the earth with fear.
verses.tsw_comparator: God cuts off the spirit of princes and is fearsome to the kings of the earth.

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated voice, qere title name and positive hearing clause.
verses.before: My voice is to God, and I cry aloud; my voice is to God, that God may hear me.
verses.after: For the music leader. According to Jeduthun. Of Asaph. A psalm. I cry aloud to God; aloud I call to God, and he listens to me.
verses.tsw_comparator: My voice is to God, and I cry aloud; my voice is to God, that God may hear me.

verses.rationale: Keeps the extended hand as prayer gesture and the refusal of comfort.
verses.before: In the day of my trouble I seek the Lord; at night my hand is stretched out and does not grow weary; my soul refuses to be comforted.
verses.after: In my distress I sought the Lord. All night my hand stayed stretched out without tiring; I refused to be comforted.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the day of my trouble I seek the Lord; at night my hand is stretched out and does not grow weary; my soul refuses to be comforted.

verses.rationale: Retains remembering as initially painful rather than immediately consoling.
verses.before: I remember God, and I groan; I meditate, and my spirit grows faint. Selah.
verses.after: I remember God and groan; I reflect, and my spirit grows faint. Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: I remember God, and I groan; I meditate, and my spirit grows faint. Selah.

verses.rationale: Keeps direct divine agency in the sleeplessness.
verses.before: You hold my eyelids open; I am troubled and cannot speak.
verses.after: You hold my eyelids open. I am so troubled that I cannot speak.
verses.tsw_comparator: You hold my eyelids open; I am troubled and cannot speak.

verses.rationale: Maintains paired days and years of recollection.
verses.before: I consider the days of old, the years long past.
verses.after: I think about the days long past, the years of ancient times.
verses.tsw_comparator: I consider the days of old, the years long past.

verses.rationale: Preserves my song and the inner search leading to questions.
verses.before: I remember my song in the night; I meditate in my heart, and my spirit searches:
verses.after: At night I remember my song; I ponder in my heart, and my spirit searches:
verses.tsw_comparator: I remember my song in the night; I meditate in my heart, and my spirit searches:

verses.rationale: Keeps the extreme temporal questions as the poet's lament.
verses.before: Will the Lord reject forever and never again show favor?
verses.after: “Will the Lord reject us forever? Will he never show favor again?
verses.tsw_comparator: Will the Lord reject forever and never again show favor?

verses.rationale: Retains love and promise as separate grounds of doubt.
verses.before: Has steadfast love ceased forever? Has the promise come to an end for generation after generation?
verses.after: Has his faithful love vanished for good? Has his promise failed for every generation?
verses.tsw_comparator: Has steadfast love ceased forever? Has the promise come to an end for generation after generation?

verses.rationale: Preserves the provocative questions without answering them within the verse.
verses.before: Has God forgotten to be gracious? Has anger shut up compassion? Selah.
verses.after: Has God forgotten to be gracious? Has anger shut away his compassion?” Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Has God forgotten to be gracious? Has anger shut up compassion? Selah.

verses.rationale: Chooses the painful-change reading of difficult shenot and halloti; notes the years/appeal alternative.
verses.before: Then I said, “This is my grief: that the right hand of the Most High has changed.”
verses.after: Then I said, “This is what wounds me: the right hand of the Most High has changed.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then I said, “This is my grief: that the right hand of the Most High has changed.”

verses.rationale: Follows qere remember, retains YAH and the shift to your.
verses.before: I will remember the deeds of the LORD; yes, I will remember your wonders from of old.
verses.after: I will remember the deeds of YAH; yes, I will remember your wonders of long ago.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will remember the deeds of the LORD; yes, I will remember your wonders from of old.

verses.rationale: Keeps both forms of sustained remembering.
verses.before: I will ponder all your work and meditate on your mighty deeds.
verses.after: I will ponder everything you have done and reflect on your great deeds.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will ponder all your work and meditate on your mighty deeds.

verses.rationale: Retains holiness and the comparative divine question.
verses.before: O God, your way is holy. What god is great like God?
verses.after: God, your way is holy. What god is as great as God?
verses.tsw_comparator: O God, your way is holy. What god is great like God?

verses.rationale: Keeps wonders and public revelation distinct.
verses.before: You are the God who works wonders; you have made your strength known among the peoples.
verses.after: You are the God who works wonders; you have made your strength known among the peoples.
verses.tsw_comparator: You are the God who works wonders; you have made your strength known among the peoples.

verses.rationale: Preserves both ancestral names and redemption's arm image.
verses.before: With your arm you redeemed your people, the children of Jacob and Joseph. Selah.
verses.after: With your arm you redeemed your people, the children of Jacob and Joseph. Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: With your arm you redeemed your people, the children of Jacob and Joseph. Selah.

verses.rationale: Maintains repeated seeing and personified cosmic waters.
verses.before: The waters saw you, O God; the waters saw you and writhed; yes, the depths trembled.
verses.after: The waters saw you, God; the waters saw you and writhed. Even the depths trembled.
verses.tsw_comparator: The waters saw you, O God; the waters saw you and writhed; yes, the depths trembled.

verses.rationale: Keeps arrows as the lightning image without replacing it completely.
verses.before: The clouds poured out water; the skies gave forth thunder; your arrows flashed on every side.
verses.after: Clouds poured down water; the skies gave their thunderous cry, and your arrows flashed back and forth.
verses.tsw_comparator: The clouds poured out water; the skies gave forth thunder; your arrows flashed on every side.

verses.rationale: Reads galgal as whirling storm, with the double earth reaction intact.
verses.before: The sound of your thunder was in the whirlwind; lightning lit up the world; the earth trembled and shook.
verses.after: Your thunder rolled in the whirlwind; lightning lit the world. The earth trembled and shook.
verses.tsw_comparator: The sound of your thunder was in the whirlwind; lightning lit up the world; the earth trembled and shook.

verses.rationale: Follows qere singular path and retains unknowable footprints.
verses.before: Your way was through the sea, your path through mighty waters, yet your footprints were not known.
verses.after: Your way ran through the sea, your path through mighty waters, but your footprints could not be found.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your way was through the sea, your path through mighty waters, yet your footprints were not known.

verses.rationale: Keeps both human leaders and the abrupt quiet shepherd conclusion.
verses.before: You led your people like a flock by the hand of Moses and Aaron.
verses.after: You led your people like a flock by the hands of Moses and Aaron.
verses.tsw_comparator: You led your people like a flock by the hand of Moses and Aaron.

verses.rationale: Keeps the teacher's first-person instruction and direct audience.
verses.before: Give ear, O my people, to my teaching; incline your ears to the words of my mouth.
verses.after: A maskil of Asaph. My people, listen to my instruction; turn your ears toward the words I speak.
verses.tsw_comparator: Give ear, O my people, to my teaching; incline your ears to the words of my mouth.

verses.rationale: Preserves mashal and riddles as the framing of history.
verses.before: I will open my mouth in a parable; I will utter riddles from of old,
verses.after: I will open my mouth with a parable; I will bring forth riddles from long ago—
verses.tsw_comparator: I will open my mouth in a parable; I will utter riddles from of old,

verses.rationale: Keeps transmission through fathers and repeated things.
verses.before: things that we have heard and known, that our ancestors have told us.
verses.after: things we have heard and known, things our fathers told us.
verses.tsw_comparator: things that we have heard and known, that our ancestors have told us.

verses.rationale: Retains their children and explicit intergenerational purpose.
verses.before: We will not hide them from their children, but tell to the coming generation the praises of the LORD, and his strength, and the wonders that he has done.
verses.after: We will not hide them from their children. We will tell the coming generation the LORD's praiseworthy deeds, his strength and the wonders he has done.
verses.tsw_comparator: We will not hide them from their children, but tell to the coming generation the praises of the LORD, and his strength, and the wonders that he has done.

verses.rationale: Preserves testimony/instruction pairing and parental obligation.
verses.before: He established a testimony in Jacob and appointed a law in Israel, which he commanded our ancestors to teach to their children,
verses.after: He established a testimony in Jacob and set instruction in Israel. He commanded our fathers to teach these things to their children,
verses.tsw_comparator: He established a testimony in Jacob and appointed a law in Israel, which he commanded our ancestors to teach to their children,

verses.rationale: Retains unborn children and the continuing chain of telling.
verses.before: that the next generation might know them, the children yet unborn, and arise and tell them to their children,
verses.after: so the next generation would know— children yet to be born— and rise to tell their own children.
verses.tsw_comparator: that the next generation might know them, the children yet unborn, and arise and tell them to their children,

verses.rationale: Keeps confidence, memory and obedience as three linked outcomes.
verses.before: so that they should set their hope in God and not forget the works of God, but keep his commandments,
verses.after: Then they would put their confidence in God, remember God's deeds and keep his commands.
verses.tsw_comparator: so that they should set their hope in God and not forget the works of God, but keep his commandments,

verses.rationale: Preserves both heart and spirit diagnoses without importing ethnic generalizations.
verses.before: and not be like their ancestors, a stubborn and rebellious generation, a generation whose heart was not steadfast, whose spirit was not faithful to God.
verses.after: They would not be like their fathers, a stubborn, rebellious generation, whose hearts were not steadfast and whose spirits were not faithful to God.
verses.tsw_comparator: and not be like their ancestors, a stubborn and rebellious generation, a generation whose heart was not steadfast, whose spirit was not faithful to God.

verses.rationale: Keeps the named tribe and reversal without inventing a battle identification.
verses.before: The Ephraimites, armed with the bow, turned back on the day of battle.
verses.after: The men of Ephraim, armed with bows, turned back on the day of battle.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Ephraimites, armed with the bow, turned back on the day of battle.

verses.rationale: Retains covenant and the walking image.
verses.before: They did not keep God’s covenant, but refused to walk according to his law.
verses.after: They did not keep God's covenant; they refused to walk in his instruction.
verses.tsw_comparator: They did not keep God’s covenant, but refused to walk according to his law.

verses.rationale: Preserves the memory failure as the narrative's recurring charge.
verses.before: They forgot his works and the wonders that he had shown them.
verses.after: They forgot his deeds and the wonders he had shown them.
verses.tsw_comparator: They forgot his works and the wonders that he had shown them.

verses.rationale: Keeps both geographic designations.
verses.before: In the sight of their ancestors he performed wonders in the land of Egypt, in the fields of Zoan.
verses.after: He worked wonders before their fathers in the land of Egypt, in the fields of Zoan.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the sight of their ancestors he performed wonders in the land of Egypt, in the fields of Zoan.

verses.rationale: Retains the piled-water image rather than making a new architectural image.
verses.before: He divided the sea and let them pass through it, and made the waters stand like a heap.
verses.after: He split the sea and led them through; he made the waters stand like a heap.
verses.tsw_comparator: He divided the sea and let them pass through it, and made the waters stand like a heap.

verses.rationale: Keeps the all-night duration and day/night pairing.
verses.before: In the daytime he led them with a cloud, and all the night with a fiery light.
verses.after: He guided them with a cloud by day and with the light of fire all night.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the daytime he led them with a cloud, and all the night with a fiery light.

verses.rationale: Preserves plural rocks and depths as the scale of water provision.
verses.before: He split rocks in the wilderness and gave them drink abundantly as from the deep.
verses.after: He split rocks in the wilderness and gave them abundant water, as from the depths.
verses.tsw_comparator: He split rocks in the wilderness and gave them drink abundantly as from the deep.

verses.rationale: Retains the crag and the descending river simile.
verses.before: He made streams come out of the rock and caused waters to flow down like rivers.
verses.after: He brought streams out of a crag and made water pour down like rivers.
verses.tsw_comparator: He made streams come out of the rock and caused waters to flow down like rivers.

verses.rationale: Keeps persistence and the divine title.
verses.before: Yet they continued to sin against him, rebelling against the Most High in the desert.
verses.after: Still they kept sinning against him, rebelling against the Most High in the dry land.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet they continued to sin against him, rebelling against the Most High in the desert.

verses.rationale: Reads nephesh contextually as appetite, with intentional testing retained.
verses.before: They tested God in their heart by demanding the food they craved.
verses.after: They tested God in their hearts by demanding food for their appetites.
verses.tsw_comparator: They tested God in their heart by demanding the food they craved.

verses.rationale: Preserves the table image and challenging question.
verses.before: They spoke against God, saying, “Can God spread a table in the wilderness?
verses.after: They spoke against God, saying, “Can God set a table in the wilderness?
verses.tsw_comparator: They spoke against God, saying, “Can God spread a table in the wilderness?

verses.rationale: Keeps their admission of one miracle within their renewed challenge.
verses.before: He struck the rock so that water gushed out— but can he also give bread or provide meat for his people?”
verses.after: He struck the rock, and water gushed out; streams overflowed. But can he also give bread? Can he provide meat for his people?”
verses.tsw_comparator: He struck the rock so that water gushed out— but can he also give bread or provide meat for his people?”

verses.rationale: Preserves anger and fire directed at the named people.
verses.before: So, when the LORD heard, he was full of wrath; a fire was kindled against Jacob, and anger rose against Israel,
verses.after: The LORD heard and was furious. Fire flared against Jacob; anger rose against Israel,
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore, when the LORD heard, he was full of wrath; a fire was kindled against Jacob, and anger rose against Israel,

verses.rationale: Keeps trust and reliance as the reason for judgment.
verses.before: because they did not believe in God and did not trust his saving power.
verses.after: because they did not trust God or rely on his saving power.
verses.tsw_comparator: because they did not believe in God and did not trust his saving power.

verses.rationale: Preserves cosmic doors and the contrast of continued provision.
verses.before: Yet he commanded the skies above and opened the doors of heaven,
verses.after: Yet he commanded the skies above and opened heaven's doors.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet he commanded the skies above and opened the doors of heaven,

verses.rationale: Retains manna and grain as related but distinct terms.
verses.before: and he rained down on them manna to eat and gave them the grain of heaven.
verses.after: He rained manna down for them to eat and gave them the grain of heaven.
verses.tsw_comparator: and he rained down on them manna to eat and gave them the grain of heaven.

verses.rationale: Keeps mighty ones rather than specifying angels without a note.
verses.before: Humans ate the bread of angels; he sent them food in abundance.
verses.after: Human beings ate the bread of mighty ones; he sent food until they had enough.
verses.tsw_comparator: Humans ate the bread of angels; he sent them food in abundance.

verses.rationale: Preserves both compass directions.
verses.before: He caused the east wind to blow in the heavens, and by his power he led out the south wind;
verses.after: He stirred up the east wind in the heavens and drove the south wind by his strength.
verses.tsw_comparator: He caused the east wind to blow in the heavens, and by his power he led out the south wind;

verses.rationale: Retains both abundance similes and unspecified birds.
verses.before: he rained meat upon them like dust, winged birds like the sand of the seas;
verses.after: He rained meat on them like dust, winged birds like sand beside the seas.
verses.tsw_comparator: he rained meat upon them like dust, winged birds like the sand of the seas;

verses.rationale: Keeps the source's singular possessive rather than silently harmonizing to their.
verses.before: he let them fall among their camp, all around their dwellings.
verses.after: He made them fall inside his camp, all around his dwellings.
verses.tsw_comparator: he let them fall in the midst of their camp, all around their dwellings.

verses.rationale: Retains satisfaction preceding judgment.
verses.before: And they ate and were filled, for he gave them what they craved.
verses.after: They ate and were thoroughly satisfied; he gave them what they craved.
verses.tsw_comparator: And they ate and were filled, for he gave them what they craved.

verses.rationale: Keeps simultaneous desire and eating, leading into divine anger.
verses.before: But before they had satisfied their desire, while the food was still in their mouths,
verses.after: But before their craving had left them, while the food was still in their mouths,
verses.tsw_comparator: But before they had satisfied their desire, while the food was still in their mouths,

verses.rationale: Preserves lethal action and the specific younger males.
verses.before: the anger of God rose against them, and he killed the strongest among them and laid low the young men of Israel.
verses.after: God's anger rose against them. He killed their strongest men and struck down Israel's young men.
verses.tsw_comparator: the anger of God rose against them, and he killed the strongest among them and laid low the young men of Israel.

verses.rationale: Retains the emphatic double failure.
verses.before: In spite of all this, they still sinned; they did not believe in his wondrous works.
verses.after: Despite all this, they kept sinning; despite his wonders, they did not trust.
verses.tsw_comparator: In spite of all this, they still sinned; they did not believe in his wondrous works.

verses.rationale: Keeps breath/transience and alarm without assigning a lifespan.
verses.before: So he made their days vanish like a breath, and their years in terror.
verses.after: So he brought their days to an end like a breath, and their years in sudden terror.
verses.tsw_comparator: So he made their days vanish like a breath, and their years in terror.

verses.rationale: Preserves death as the occasion of the survivors' turning.
verses.before: When he killed them, they sought him; they repented and sought God earnestly.
verses.after: When he killed them, they sought him; they returned and searched earnestly for God.
verses.tsw_comparator: When he killed them, they sought him; they repented and sought God earnestly.

verses.rationale: Retains rock, divine title and redeemer.
verses.before: They remembered that God was their rock, the Most High God their redeemer.
verses.after: They remembered that God was their rock, that God Most High was their redeemer.
verses.tsw_comparator: They remembered that God was their rock, the Most High God their redeemer.

verses.rationale: Keeps mouth/tongue parallelism and deceptive religious speech.
verses.before: But they flattered him with their mouths; they lied to him with their tongues.
verses.after: But they tried to flatter him with their mouths and lied to him with their tongues.
verses.tsw_comparator: But they flattered him with their mouths; they lied to him with their tongues.

verses.rationale: Links steadfast hearts to the earlier generation warning.
verses.before: Their heart was not steadfast toward him; they were not faithful to his covenant.
verses.after: Their hearts were not steadfast toward him; they were not faithful to his covenant.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their heart was not steadfast toward him; they were not faithful to his covenant.

verses.rationale: Retains atonement, restraint and repeated mercy without erasing judgment.
verses.before: Yet he, being compassionate, atoned for their iniquity and did not destroy them; he restrained his anger often and did not stir up all his wrath.
verses.after: Yet he was compassionate: he made atonement for their wrongdoing instead of destroying them. Again and again he turned back his anger and did not unleash all his fury.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet he, being compassionate, atoned for their iniquity and did not destroy them; he restrained his anger often and did not stir up all his wrath.

verses.rationale: Keeps flesh and wind as human fragility images.
verses.before: He remembered that they were flesh, a wind that passes and does not return.
verses.after: He remembered that they were only flesh, a passing wind that does not return.
verses.tsw_comparator: He remembered that they were flesh, a wind that passes and does not return.

verses.rationale: Retains divine grief as well as human rebellion.
verses.before: How often they rebelled against him in the wilderness and grieved him in the desert!
verses.after: How often they rebelled against him in the wilderness and grieved him in the desert!
verses.tsw_comparator: How often they rebelled against him in the wilderness and grieved him in the desert!

verses.rationale: Chooses pained for the difficult verb, preserving the specific divine title.
verses.before: They tested God again and again and provoked the Holy One of Israel.
verses.after: Again and again they tested God and pained the Holy One of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: They tested God again and again and provoked the Holy One of Israel.

verses.rationale: Keeps hand as power image and introduces retrospective rescue.
verses.before: They did not remember his power or the day when he redeemed them from the foe,
verses.after: They did not remember his hand, the day he redeemed them from the foe,
verses.tsw_comparator: They did not remember his power or the day when he redeemed them from the foe,

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated geography and signs/wonders pairing.
verses.before: when he performed his signs in Egypt and his marvels in the fields of Zoan.
verses.after: when he displayed his signs in Egypt and his wonders in the fields of Zoan.
verses.tsw_comparator: when he performed his signs in Egypt and his marvels in the fields of Zoan.

verses.rationale: Retains plural watercourses rather than naming only the Nile.
verses.before: He turned their rivers to blood, so that they could not drink of their streams.
verses.after: He turned their rivers to blood; they could not drink from their streams.
verses.tsw_comparator: He turned their rivers to blood, so that they could not drink of their streams.

verses.rationale: Keeps the poem's order and destructive hyperbole.
verses.before: He sent among them swarms of flies, which devoured them, and frogs, which destroyed them.
verses.after: He sent swarms of flies that devoured them and frogs that brought them ruin.
verses.tsw_comparator: He sent among them swarms of flies, which devoured them, and frogs, which destroyed them.

verses.rationale: Preserves two locust terms and their agricultural losses.
verses.before: He gave their crops to the locust, and the fruit of their labor to the grasshopper.
verses.after: He gave their crops to the devouring locust, the fruit of their labor to the swarming locust.
verses.tsw_comparator: He gave their crops to the locust, and the fruit of their labor to the grasshopper.

verses.rationale: Keeps frost as a qualified reading of the rare destructive-weather term.
verses.before: He destroyed their vines with hail and their sycamores with frost.
verses.after: He killed their vines with hail and their sycamore figs with frost.
verses.tsw_comparator: He destroyed their vines with hail and their sycamores with frost.

verses.rationale: Preserves hail and fiery bolts without harmonizing the list to Exodus.
verses.before: He gave over their cattle to the hail and their flocks to thunderbolts.
verses.after: He handed their cattle over to hail, their livestock to bolts of fire.
verses.tsw_comparator: He gave over their cattle to the hail and their flocks to thunderbolts.

verses.rationale: Retains the wrath list and harmful messengers without making them morally evil spirits.
verses.before: He let loose on them his burning anger, wrath, indignation, and distress, a company of destroying angels.
verses.after: He sent his burning anger against them— fury, indignation and distress— a company of messengers bringing disaster.
verses.tsw_comparator: He let loose on them his burning anger, wrath, indignation, and distress, a company of destroying angels.

verses.rationale: Keeps the path image and explicit lethal agency.
verses.before: He made a path for his anger; he did not spare them from death but gave their lives over to plague.
verses.after: He cleared a path for his anger. He did not spare their lives from death but handed them over to plague.
verses.tsw_comparator: He made a path for his anger; he did not spare them from death but gave their lives over to plague.

verses.rationale: Preserves firstborn, reproductive strength and ancestral designation Ham.
verses.before: He struck down every firstborn in Egypt, the firstfruits of their strength in the tents of Ham.
verses.after: He struck every firstborn in Egypt, the first fruits of their strength in the tents of Ham.
verses.tsw_comparator: He struck down every firstborn in Egypt, the firstfruits of their strength in the tents of Ham.

verses.rationale: Retains paired shepherd images.
verses.before: Then he led out his people like sheep and guided them in the wilderness like a flock.
verses.after: Then he brought his people out like sheep and guided them like a flock through the wilderness.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he led out his people like sheep and guided them in the wilderness like a flock.

verses.rationale: Keeps the contrast of safety and drowning without adding detail.
verses.before: He led them in safety, so that they were not afraid, but the sea overwhelmed their enemies.
verses.after: He led them safely, so they were not afraid, but the sea covered their enemies.
verses.tsw_comparator: He led them in safety, so that they were not afraid, but the sea overwhelmed their enemies.

verses.rationale: Preserves mountain and right-hand acquisition.
verses.before: And he brought them to his holy land, to the mountain his right hand had won.
verses.after: He brought them to his holy territory, to this mountain his right hand had acquired.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he brought them to his holy land, to the mountain his right hand had won.

verses.rationale: Keeps dispossession, allocation and occupied dwellings explicit.
verses.before: He drove out nations before them; he allotted them for a possession and settled the tribes of Israel in their tents.
verses.after: He drove nations out before them, allotted their land as an inheritance by measuring line, and settled Israel's tribes in their tents.
verses.tsw_comparator: He drove out nations before them; he allotted them for a possession and settled the tribes of Israel in their tents.

verses.rationale: Preserves the renewed failure after settlement.
verses.before: Yet they tested and rebelled against the Most High God and did not keep his testimonies,
verses.after: But they tested God Most High and rebelled against him; they did not keep his testimonies.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet they tested and rebelled against the Most High God and did not keep his testimonies,

verses.rationale: Keeps the defective bow metaphor and ancestral comparison.
verses.before: but turned away and acted treacherously like their ancestors; they twisted like a deceitful bow.
verses.after: They turned away and acted treacherously like their fathers; they twisted aside like an unreliable bow.
verses.tsw_comparator: but turned away and acted treacherously like their ancestors; they twisted like a deceitful bow.

verses.rationale: Retains cultic high places and jealousy rather than reducing both to generic wrongdoing.
verses.before: For they provoked him to anger with their high places; they moved him to jealousy with their idols.
verses.after: They angered him with their high places and provoked his jealousy with their carved images.
verses.tsw_comparator: For they provoked him to anger with their high places; they moved him to jealousy with their idols.

verses.rationale: Preserves the severe rejection claim without treating it as the poem's final word.
verses.before: When God heard, he was full of wrath, and he utterly rejected Israel.
verses.after: God heard and was furious; he utterly rejected Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: When God heard, he was full of wrath, and he utterly rejected Israel.

verses.rationale: Keeps the site and divine dwelling among people.
verses.before: He forsook his dwelling at Shiloh, the tent where he dwelt among humanity,
verses.after: He abandoned his dwelling at Shiloh, the tent where he had lived among human beings.
verses.tsw_comparator: He forsook his dwelling at Shiloh, the tent where he dwelt among humanity,

verses.rationale: Retains the metaphorical strength/splendor language; notes the ark association.
verses.before: and delivered his power to captivity, his glory to the hand of the foe.
verses.after: He gave his strength into captivity, his splendor into the enemy's hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: and delivered his power to captivity, his glory to the hand of the foe.

verses.rationale: Keeps violent judgment and inheritance as his people.
verses.before: He gave his people over to the sword and vented his wrath on his inheritance.
verses.after: He handed his people over to the sword; he was furious with his own inheritance.
verses.tsw_comparator: He gave his people over to the sword and vented his wrath on his inheritance.

verses.rationale: Retains gender-specific losses and the suppressed marriage celebration.
verses.before: Fire devoured their young men, and their young women had no marriage song.
verses.after: Fire consumed their young men, and their young women had no wedding songs.
verses.tsw_comparator: Fire devoured their young men, and their young women had no marriage song.

verses.rationale: Keeps absent mourning without inventing a reason.
verses.before: Their priests fell by the sword, and their widows made no lamentation.
verses.after: Their priests fell by the sword, and their widows did not weep.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their priests fell by the sword, and their widows made no lamentation.

verses.rationale: Preserves the striking wine and awakening simile without sanitizing it.
verses.before: Then the Lord awoke as from sleep, like a warrior shouting because of wine.
verses.after: Then the Lord awoke as though from sleep, like a warrior shouting after wine.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the Lord awoke as from sleep, like a warrior shouting because of wine.

verses.rationale: Retains the ambiguous rearward blow and lasting disgrace.
verses.before: He struck his enemies backward; he put them to perpetual shame.
verses.after: He struck his enemies from behind and put them to lasting shame.
verses.tsw_comparator: He struck his enemies backward; he put them to perpetual shame.

verses.rationale: Keeps Joseph and Ephraim distinct within the contrast.
verses.before: He rejected the tent of Joseph; he did not choose the tribe of Ephraim,
verses.after: He rejected Joseph's tent and did not choose the tribe of Ephraim.
verses.tsw_comparator: He rejected the tent of Joseph; he did not choose the tribe of Ephraim,

verses.rationale: Preserves the two objects of choice and love.
verses.before: but he chose the tribe of Judah, Mount Zion, which he loves.
verses.after: Instead he chose the tribe of Judah, Mount Zion, which he loved.
verses.tsw_comparator: but he chose the tribe of Judah, Mount Zion, which he loves.

verses.rationale: Retains heights rather than specifying mountains absent from this noun.
verses.before: He built his sanctuary like the heights, like the earth, which he has founded forever.
verses.after: He built his sanctuary like the heights, like the earth he established forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: He built his sanctuary like the heights, like the earth, which he has founded forever.

verses.rationale: Keeps David's election and humble shepherd setting.
verses.before: He chose David his servant and took him from the sheepfolds;
verses.after: He chose David his servant and took him from the sheepfolds.
verses.tsw_comparator: He chose David his servant and took him from the sheepfolds;

verses.rationale: Preserves nursing sheep and the transfer to human shepherding.
verses.before: from following the nursing ewes he brought him to shepherd Jacob his people, Israel his inheritance.
verses.after: From tending nursing ewes he brought him to shepherd Jacob his people, Israel his inheritance.
verses.tsw_comparator: from following the nursing ewes he brought him to shepherd Jacob his people, Israel his inheritance.

verses.rationale: Retains heart integrity and hand skill as the concluding pair.
verses.before: With upright heart he shepherded them and guided them with skillful hand.
verses.after: He shepherded them with an undivided heart and guided them with skillful hands.
verses.tsw_comparator: With upright heart he shepherded them and guided them with skillful hand.

verses.rationale: Retains all three dimensions of invasion, desecration and destruction.
verses.before: A psalm of Asaph. God, nations have entered your inheritance; they have defiled your holy temple; they have made Jerusalem a ruin.
verses.after: A psalm of Asaph. God, nations have invaded your inheritance. They have defiled your holy temple and reduced Jerusalem to rubble.
verses.tsw_comparator: A psalm of Asaph. God, nations have entered your inheritance; they have defiled your holy temple; they have made Jerusalem a ruin.

verses.rationale: Preserves the unburied bodies and physical violence.
verses.before: They have given the bodies of your servants as food to the birds of the heavens, the flesh of your faithful ones to the wild animals of the earth.
verses.after: They have given your servants' corpses to the birds of the sky for food, the flesh of your faithful people to the beasts of the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: They have given the bodies of your servants as food to the birds of the heavens, the flesh of your faithful ones to the wild animals of the earth.

verses.rationale: Keeps blood/water comparison and missing burial.
verses.before: They have poured out their blood like water all around Jerusalem, with no one to bury them.
verses.after: They have poured out their blood like water around Jerusalem, and no one is left to bury them.
verses.tsw_comparator: They have poured out their blood like water all around Jerusalem, with no one to bury them.

verses.rationale: Retains the surrounding community's ridicule.
verses.before: We have become a reproach to our neighbors, mockery and scorn to those around us.
verses.after: Our neighbors treat us with contempt; those around us mock and jeer.
verses.tsw_comparator: We have become a reproach to our neighbors, mockery and scorn to those around us.

verses.rationale: Preserves duration questions and jealousy as fire.
verses.before: How long, LORD? Will you be angry forever? Will your jealousy burn like fire?
verses.after: How long, LORD? Will you be angry forever? Will your jealousy keep burning like fire?
verses.tsw_comparator: How long, LORD? Will you be angry forever? Will your jealousy burn like fire?

verses.rationale: Keeps the requested redirection of divine wrath explicit.
verses.before: Pour out your wrath on the nations that do not know you, on the kingdoms that do not call on your name.
verses.after: Pour out your fury on the nations that do not know you, on kingdoms that do not call on your name.
verses.tsw_comparator: Pour out your wrath on the nations that do not know you, on the kingdoms that do not call on your name.

verses.rationale: Renders the collective foes naturally while retaining the devouring metaphor.
verses.before: For they have devoured Jacob and laid waste his dwelling place.
verses.after: For they have devoured Jacob and devastated his home.
verses.tsw_comparator: For they have devoured Jacob and laid waste his dwelling place.

verses.rationale: Leaves past/ancestral wrongdoing scope open in note and preserves urgent compassion.
verses.before: Do not remember against us the iniquities of former generations. May your mercies quickly meet us, for we have been brought very low.
verses.after: Do not hold past wrongs against us. Let your compassion hurry to meet us, for we have been brought very low.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not remember against us the iniquities of former generations. May your mercies quickly meet us, for we have been brought very low.

verses.rationale: Keeps doubled name appeal and atonement term.
verses.before: Help us, God of our salvation, for the glory of your name; deliver us and atone for our sins, for the sake of your name.
verses.after: Help us, God our savior, for the glory of your name. Rescue us and make atonement for our sins, for the sake of your name.
verses.tsw_comparator: Help us, God of our salvation, for the glory of your name; deliver us and atone for our sins, for the sake of your name.

verses.rationale: Preserves the requested visible vengeance and qere nations.
verses.before: Why should the nations say, “Where is their God?” Let the vengeance for the blood of your servants that was poured out be known among the nations— among the nations before our eyes.
verses.after: Why should the nations ask, “Where is their God?” Before our eyes, let the nations see you avenge your servants' spilled blood.
verses.tsw_comparator: Why should the nations say, “Where is their God?” Let the vengeance for the blood of your servants that was poured out be known among the nations— among the nations before our eyes.

verses.rationale: Retains prisoner, arm and threatened lives without changing them to metaphors.
verses.before: May the groaning of the prisoner come before you; according to the greatness of your arm, preserve those doomed to die.
verses.after: Let the prisoner's groan reach you. By the strength of your mighty arm, keep alive those marked for death.
verses.tsw_comparator: May the groaning of the prisoner come before you; according to the greatness of your arm, preserve those doomed to die.

verses.rationale: Preserves exact sevenfold retaliation and lap image.
verses.before: Return sevenfold into the laps of our neighbors the reproach with which they have reproached you, Lord.
verses.after: Lord, pay our neighbors back sevenfold, right into their laps, for the contempt they have shown you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Return sevenfold into the laps of our neighbors the reproach with which they have reproached you, Lord.

verses.rationale: Keeps flock identity and intergenerational praise promise.
verses.before: Then we, your people and the sheep of your pasture, will give thanks to you forever; from generation to generation we will tell of your praise.
verses.after: Then we, your people, the sheep of your pasture, will thank you forever. Generation after generation, we will tell of your praise.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then we, your people and the sheep of your pasture, will give thanks to you forever; from generation to generation we will tell of your praise.

verses.rationale: Preserves the title's uncertain musical terms and shepherd/throne pairing.
verses.before: Give ear, O Shepherd of Israel, you who lead Joseph like a flock; you who are enthroned upon the cherubim, shine forth.
verses.after: For the music leader. “Lilies.” A testimony. Of Asaph. A psalm. Shepherd of Israel, listen— you who lead Joseph like a flock! You who sit enthroned above the cherubim, shine forth!
verses.tsw_comparator: Give ear, O Shepherd of Israel, you who lead Joseph like a flock; you who are enthroned upon the cherubim, shine forth.

verses.rationale: Keeps all three tribes in their order.
verses.before: Before Ephraim and Benjamin and Manasseh, stir up your might and come to save us.
verses.after: Before Ephraim, Benjamin and Manasseh, rouse your strength and come to save us.
verses.tsw_comparator: Before Ephraim and Benjamin and Manasseh, stir up your might and come to save us.

verses.rationale: Establishes the recurring refrain without later expanded divine titles.
verses.before: Restore us, O God; let your face shine, that we may be saved.
verses.after: God, restore us; let your face shine, and we will be saved.
verses.tsw_comparator: Restore us, O God; let your face shine, that we may be saved.

verses.rationale: Preserves smoking anger specifically against prayer.
verses.before: O LORD God of hosts, how long will you be angry with the prayers of your people?
verses.after: LORD, God of Armies, how long will your anger smoke against your people's prayer?
verses.tsw_comparator: O LORD God of hosts, how long will you be angry with the prayers of your people?

verses.rationale: Keeps tears as both food and drink and the uncertain measure rather than inventing a volume.
verses.before: You have fed them with the bread of tears and given them tears to drink in full measure.
verses.after: You have fed them bread made of tears and given them tears to drink by the measure.
verses.tsw_comparator: You have fed them with the bread of tears and given them tears to drink in full measure.

verses.rationale: Keeps conflict and the source's reflexive laughter phrase.
verses.before: You make us an object of contention for our neighbors, and our enemies laugh among themselves.
verses.after: You have made us a cause of strife among our neighbors; our enemies laugh among themselves.
verses.tsw_comparator: You make us an object of contention for our neighbors, and our enemies laugh among themselves.

verses.rationale: Retains the expanded refrain title with identical remaining wording.
verses.before: Restore us, O God of hosts; let your face shine, that we may be saved.
verses.after: God of Armies, restore us; let your face shine, and we will be saved.
verses.tsw_comparator: Restore us, O God of hosts; let your face shine, that we may be saved.

verses.rationale: Keeps the sustained vine image and dispossession.
verses.before: You brought a vine out of Egypt; you drove out nations and planted it.
verses.after: You brought a vine out of Egypt; you drove out nations and planted it.
verses.tsw_comparator: You brought a vine out of Egypt; you drove out nations and planted it.

verses.rationale: Retains preparation, roots and spreading growth.
verses.before: You cleared the ground for it; it took deep root and filled the land.
verses.after: You cleared a place for it; it took deep root and filled the land.
verses.tsw_comparator: You cleared the ground for it; it took deep root and filled the land.

verses.rationale: Reads cedars of God as mighty while retaining the vine's immense scale.
verses.before: The mountains were covered with its shade, and the mighty cedars with its branches.
verses.after: Mountains lay under its shade, and mighty cedars beneath its branches.
verses.tsw_comparator: The mountains were covered with its shade, and the mighty cedars with its branches.

verses.rationale: Preserves the two geographic boundaries and capitalized conventional River.
verses.before: It sent out its branches to the sea and its shoots to the River.
verses.after: It sent its branches as far as the sea, its shoots as far as the River.
verses.tsw_comparator: It sent out its branches to the sea and its shoots to the River.

verses.rationale: Keeps the direct accusation and exposed fruit.
verses.before: Why then have you broken down its walls, so that everyone who pass along the way pluck its fruit?
verses.after: Why have you broken down its walls, so that everyone passing by plucks its fruit?
verses.tsw_comparator: Why then have you broken down its walls, so that all who pass along the way pluck its fruit?

verses.rationale: Preserves the specific boar and wider field animals.
verses.before: The boar from the forest ravages it, and all that move in the field feed on it.
verses.after: A boar from the forest tears it apart; creatures of the field feed on it.
verses.tsw_comparator: The boar from the forest ravages it, and all that move in the field feed on it.

verses.rationale: Keeps return answering restore and the request to attend the vine.
verses.before: Turn again, O God of hosts! Look down from heaven and see; have regard for this vine,
verses.after: God of Armies, please return! Look down from heaven and see; care for this vine,
verses.tsw_comparator: Turn again, O God of hosts! Look down from heaven and see; have regard for this vine,

verses.rationale: Retains the difficult shift from plant to son and notes its ambiguity.
verses.before: the stock that your right hand planted, and the son whom you made strong for yourself.
verses.after: the stock your right hand planted, the son you made strong for yourself.
verses.tsw_comparator: the stock that your right hand planted, and the son whom you made strong for yourself.

verses.rationale: Preserves the singular vine to plural they change rather than hiding it.
verses.before: It is burned with fire, it is cut down; they perish at the rebuke of your face.
verses.after: It is burned with fire and cut down; at the rebuke of your face, they perish.
verses.tsw_comparator: It is burned with fire, it is cut down; they perish at the rebuke of your face.

verses.rationale: Keeps man/son-of-man parallelism without settling a later identification.
verses.before: But let your hand be upon the man of your right hand, the son of man whom you have made strong for yourself.
verses.after: Let your hand rest on the man at your right hand, the son of man you made strong for yourself.
verses.tsw_comparator: But let your hand be upon the man of your right hand, the son of man whom you have made strong for yourself.

verses.rationale: Retains community pledge and dependence on renewed life.
verses.before: Then we will not turn back from you; give us life, and we will call upon your name.
verses.after: Then we will not turn away from you. Give us life, and we will call on your name.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then we will not turn back from you; give us life, and we will call upon your name.

verses.rationale: Preserves the fullest divine title at the final refrain.
verses.before: Restore us, O LORD God of hosts; let your face shine, that we may be saved.
verses.after: LORD, God of Armies, restore us; let your face shine, and we will be saved.
verses.tsw_comparator: Restore us, O LORD God of hosts; let your face shine, that we may be saved.

verses.rationale: Retains the uncertain Gittith label and paired praise calls.
verses.before: Sing aloud to God our strength; shout for joy to the God of Jacob.
verses.after: For the music leader. According to the Gittith. Of Asaph. Sing out to God our strength; shout for joy to the God of Jacob.
verses.tsw_comparator: Sing aloud to God our strength; shout for joy to the God of Jacob.

verses.rationale: Keeps the distinct instruments and pleasant lyre quality.
verses.before: Raise a song; sound the tambourine, the sweet lyre with the harp.
verses.after: Strike up a song and sound the tambourine, the sweet lyre together with the harp.
verses.tsw_comparator: Raise a song; sound the tambourine, the sweet lyre with the harp.

verses.rationale: Retains lunar markers; notes uncertainty about keseh and festival identification.
verses.before: Blow the horn at the new moon, at the full moon, for our feast day.
verses.after: Blow the ram's horn at the new moon, at the full moon, on our festival day.
verses.tsw_comparator: Blow the horn at the new moon, at the full moon, for our feast day.

verses.rationale: Preserves parallel legal descriptions.
verses.before: For this is a statute for Israel, an ordinance of the God of Jacob.
verses.after: This is a statute for Israel, a ruling of the God of Jacob.
verses.tsw_comparator: For this is a statute for Israel, an ordinance of the God of Jacob.

verses.rationale: Preserves Joseph and the ambiguous departure phrase, marking the voice transition.
verses.before: God established it as a testimony in Joseph when God went out against the land of Egypt. I heard a language I did not know:
verses.after: He established it as a testimony in Joseph when he went out against the land of Egypt. I hear a language I did not know:
verses.tsw_comparator: God established it as a testimony in Joseph when God went out against the land of Egypt. I heard a language I did not know:

verses.rationale: Retains the third-person laborer and concrete forced-labor objects.
verses.before: “I relieved your shoulder of the burden; your hands were freed from the basket.
verses.after: “I lifted the burden from his shoulder; his hands were freed from the basket.
verses.tsw_comparator: “I relieved your shoulder of the burden; your hands were freed from the basket.

verses.rationale: Keeps the shift to you, thunder concealment and named test site.
verses.before: In distress you called, and I rescued you; I answered you from the hiding place of thunder; I tested you at the waters of Meribah. Selah.
verses.after: You called in distress, and I rescued you. I answered you from thunder's hiding place; I tested you at the waters of Meribah. Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: In distress you called, and I rescued you; I answered you from the hiding place of thunder; I tested you at the waters of Meribah. Selah.

verses.rationale: Preserves warning and the longing conditional appeal.
verses.before: Hear, my people, and I will warn you. O Israel, if only you would listen to me!
verses.after: Listen, my people, while I warn you. Israel, if only you would listen to me!
verses.tsw_comparator: Hear, my people, and I will warn you. O Israel, if only you would listen to me!

verses.rationale: Keeps both prohibition clauses.
verses.before: There will be no strange god among you; you will not bow down to a foreign god.
verses.after: There must be no strange god among you; you must not bow down to a foreign god.
verses.tsw_comparator: There shall be no strange god among you; you shall not bow down to a foreign god.

verses.rationale: Retains exodus identification and feeding promise image.
verses.before: I am the LORD your God, who brought you up from the land of Egypt. Open your mouth wide, and I will fill it.
verses.after: I am the LORD your God, who brought you up from Egypt. Open your mouth wide, and I will fill it.
verses.tsw_comparator: I am the LORD your God, who brought you up from the land of Egypt. Open your mouth wide, and I will fill it.

verses.rationale: Keeps the emphatic refusal beyond simple inattentiveness.
verses.before: But my people did not listen to my voice; Israel would not yield to me.
verses.after: But my people did not listen to my voice; Israel would have none of me.
verses.tsw_comparator: But my people did not listen to my voice; Israel would not yield to me.

verses.rationale: Retains handing over to self-chosen counsel.
verses.before: So I gave them over to the stubbornness of their hearts, to walk in their own counsels.
verses.after: So I let them follow their stubborn hearts, to walk by their own plans.
verses.tsw_comparator: So I gave them over to the stubbornness of their hearts, to walk in their own counsels.

verses.rationale: Repeats longing and walking language consistently.
verses.before: If only my people would listen to me, if Israel would walk in my ways!
verses.after: If only my people would listen to me, if only Israel would walk in my ways!
verses.tsw_comparator: If only my people would listen to me, if Israel would walk in my ways!

verses.rationale: Keeps speed and the divine hand's redirected action.
verses.before: I would soon subdue their enemies and turn my hand against their foes.
verses.after: I would soon subdue their enemies and turn my hand against their foes.
verses.tsw_comparator: I would soon subdue their enemies and turn my hand against their foes.

verses.rationale: Preserves ambiguous their time rather than inserting punishment or prosperity as certain.
verses.before: People who hate the LORD would cringe before God, and their time would be forever.
verses.after: Those who hate the LORD would cringe before him, and their time would last forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: Those who hate the LORD would cringe before God, and their time would be forever.

verses.rationale: Preserves he-to-I and people-to-you shifts; makes collective Israel explicit for the singular recipient.
verses.before: I would feed Israel with the finest wheat, and with honey from the rock I would satisfy you.”
verses.after: He would feed his people the finest wheat, and I would satisfy you with honey from the rock.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I would feed Israel with the finest wheat, and with honey from the rock I would satisfy you.”

verses.rationale: Preserves gods and assembly rather than resolving the identity as human judges.
verses.before: God stands in the divine council; among the gods, God judges:
verses.after: A psalm of Asaph. God stands in the divine assembly; among the gods he gives judgment:
verses.tsw_comparator: God stands in the divine council; in the midst of the gods, God judges:

verses.rationale: Keeps the divine rebuke and judicial partiality.
verses.before: “How long will you judge unjustly and show partiality to the wicked? Selah.
verses.after: “How long will you judge unjustly and favor the wicked? Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: “How long will you judge unjustly and show partiality to the wicked? Selah.

verses.rationale: Preserves the vulnerable groups and legal vindication.
verses.before: Give justice to the weak and the orphan; uphold the right of the afflicted and the destitute.
verses.after: Give justice to the weak and the fatherless; uphold the rights of the afflicted and the poor.
verses.tsw_comparator: Give justice to the weak and the orphan; uphold the right of the afflicted and the destitute.

verses.rationale: Retains active rescue alongside judgment.
verses.before: Rescue the weak and the needy; deliver them from the hand of the wicked.”
verses.after: Rescue the weak and the needy; free them from the hand of the wicked.
verses.tsw_comparator: Rescue the weak and the needy; deliver them from the hand of the wicked.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the shift to they and cosmic consequences.
verses.before: They do not know, and they do not understand; they walk about in darkness. All the foundations of the earth are shaken.
verses.after: They neither know nor understand; they walk about in darkness. All the foundations of the earth are shaking.
verses.tsw_comparator: They do not know, and they do not understand; they walk about in darkness. All the foundations of the earth are shaken.

verses.rationale: Retains the stated divine designations and gender-specific sons.
verses.before: I said, “You are gods, children of the Most High, all of you;
verses.after: I said, ‘You are gods, all of you sons of the Most High.’
verses.tsw_comparator: I said, “You are gods, children of the Most High, all of you;

verses.rationale: Preserves the mortality verdict without defining the judged beings in advance.
verses.before: yet like human beings you will die, and like one of the princes you will fall.”
verses.after: Yet you will die like human beings; you will fall like any ruler.”
verses.tsw_comparator: yet like human beings you shall die, and like one of the princes you shall fall.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the community's closing appeal and inheritance of nations.
verses.before: Rise up, O God; judge the earth, for you will inherit all the nations.
verses.after: Rise, God, and judge the earth, for all the nations are yours to inherit.
verses.tsw_comparator: Rise up, O God; judge the earth, for you shall inherit all the nations.

verses.rationale: Preserves three urgent pleas rather than collapsing the repetition.
verses.before: O God, do not remain silent; do not be quiet, and do not be still, O God.
verses.after: A song. A psalm of Asaph. God, do not stay silent! Do not be deaf or still, God!
verses.tsw_comparator: O God, do not remain silent; do not be quiet, and do not be still, O God.

verses.rationale: Keeps the noise and threatening posture.
verses.before: For look, your enemies are in an uproar; people who hate you have raised their heads.
verses.after: Look, your enemies are in an uproar; those who hate you lift their heads.
verses.tsw_comparator: For look, your enemies are in an uproar; those who hate you have raised their heads.

verses.rationale: Retains the protected people's identity and deliberate plotting.
verses.before: They make crafty plans against your people and conspire against those you treasure.
verses.after: They devise cunning plans against your people; they conspire against those you shelter.
verses.tsw_comparator: They make crafty plans against your people and conspire against those you treasure.

verses.rationale: Preserves the explicit extermination threat and memory erasure.
verses.before: They say, “Come, let us wipe them out as a nation, so that the name of Israel is remembered no more.”
verses.after: “Come,” they say, “let us wipe them out as a nation, so Israel's name will never be remembered again.”
verses.tsw_comparator: They say, “Come, let us wipe them out as a nation, so that the name of Israel is remembered no more.”

verses.rationale: Retains covenant even for the hostile alliance.
verses.before: For they conspire together with one heart; against you they make a covenant:
verses.after: They plot with a single purpose; they have made a covenant against you:
verses.tsw_comparator: For they conspire together with one heart; against you they make a covenant:

verses.rationale: Keeps all four named groups and Edom's tents.
verses.before: the tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites, Moab and the Hagrites,
verses.after: the tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites, Moab and the Hagrites,
verses.tsw_comparator: the tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites, Moab and the Hagrites,

verses.rationale: Preserves place and people distinctions without modern equivalents.
verses.before: Gebal and Ammon and Amalek, Philistia with the inhabitants of Tyre;
verses.after: Gebal, Ammon and Amalek, Philistia with the people of Tyre.
verses.tsw_comparator: Gebal and Ammon and Amalek, Philistia with the inhabitants of Tyre;

verses.rationale: Retains the arm image and Lot's descendants.
verses.before: Assyria also has joined them; they have become an arm for the children of Lot. Selah.
verses.after: Assyria has joined them too, lending its arm to the descendants of Lot. Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Assyria also has joined them; they have become an arm for the children of Lot. Selah.

verses.rationale: Keeps the historical comparisons and named watercourse.
verses.before: Do to them as you did to Midian, as to Sisera and Jabin at the river Kishon,
verses.after: Do to them what you did to Midian, to Sisera and Jabin at the Kishon stream.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do to them as you did to Midian, as to Sisera and Jabin at the river Kishon,

verses.rationale: Preserves the graphic corpse image.
verses.before: who were destroyed at En-dor and became dung for the ground.
verses.after: They were destroyed at En-dor; they became manure for the ground.
verses.tsw_comparator: who were destroyed at En-dor and became dung for the ground.

verses.rationale: Retains all four names and the nobles/princes parallel.
verses.before: Make their nobles like Oreb and Zeeb, all their princes like Zebah and Zalmunna,
verses.after: Make their nobles like Oreb and Zeeb, all their princes like Zebah and Zalmunna,
verses.tsw_comparator: Make their nobles like Oreb and Zeeb, all their princes like Zebah and Zalmunna,

verses.rationale: Keeps pastoral territory and the enemies' claimed possession.
verses.before: who said, “Let us take for ourselves the pastures of God.”
verses.after: who said, “Let us take God's pastures as our own possession.”
verses.tsw_comparator: who said, “Let us take for ourselves the pastures of God.”

verses.rationale: Chooses windblown plant for galgal and retains both lightness images.
verses.before: My God, make them like tumbleweed, like chaff before the wind.
verses.after: My God, make them like whirling tumbleweed, like straw before the wind.
verses.tsw_comparator: My God, make them like tumbleweed, like chaff before the wind.

verses.rationale: Preserves the spread of destructive fire.
verses.before: As fire burns a forest, and as flame sets mountains ablaze,
verses.after: As fire burns a forest, as flame sets mountains ablaze,
verses.tsw_comparator: As fire burns a forest, and as flame sets mountains ablaze,

verses.rationale: Keeps the direct petition for terror and pursuit.
verses.before: so pursue them with your tempest and terrify them with your storm.
verses.after: so pursue them with your storm and terrify them with your whirlwind.
verses.tsw_comparator: so pursue them with your tempest and terrify them with your storm.

verses.rationale: Preserves seeking the name as a purpose within the curse.
verses.before: Fill their faces with shame, so that they may seek your name, O LORD.
verses.after: Fill their faces with disgrace so that they seek your name, LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Fill their faces with shame, so that they may seek your name, O LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps the severe competing demand without harmonizing it to verse 16.
verses.before: Let them be ashamed and dismayed forever; let them be disgraced and perish.
verses.after: Let them be ashamed and terrified forever; let them be disgraced and perish.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let them be ashamed and dismayed forever; let them be disgraced and perish.

verses.rationale: Retains name, exclusive claim and worldwide scope.
verses.before: Let them know that you alone— whose name is the LORD— are Most High over all the earth.
verses.after: Let them know that you alone, whose name is the LORD, are Most High over all the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let them know that you alone— whose name is the LORD— are Most High over all the earth.

verses.rationale: Keeps plural dwellings and title attribution.
verses.before: How lovely are your dwellings, O LORD of Hosts!
verses.after: For the music leader. According to the Gittith. Of the sons of Korah. A psalm. How beloved are your dwellings, LORD of Armies!
verses.tsw_comparator: How lovely are your dwellings, O LORD of Hosts!

verses.rationale: Retains the embodied longing and living divine title.
verses.before: My soul longs, yes, even faints for the courts of the LORD. My heart and my flesh sing for joy to the living God.
verses.after: I long for the LORD's courts until I grow faint; my heart and my flesh cry out to the living God.
verses.tsw_comparator: My soul longs, yes, even faints for the courts of the LORD. My heart and my flesh sing for joy to the living God.

verses.rationale: Preserves bird/maternal nest imagery and altar proximity without asserting nests on burning altars.
verses.before: Even the bird finds a home, and the swallow a nest for herself, where she may lay her young, near your altars, O LORD of Hosts, my King and my God.
verses.after: Even a bird finds a home, and a swallow a nest for her young, near your altars, LORD of Armies, my king and my God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Even the bird finds a home, and the swallow a nest for herself, where she may lay her young, near your altars, O LORD of Hosts, my King and my God.

verses.rationale: Retains continuing praise and the beatitude pattern.
verses.before: Happy are people who dwell in your house; they are ever praising you. Selah.
verses.after: How fortunate are those who live in your house! They keep praising you. Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Happy are those who dwell in your house; they are ever praising you. Selah.

verses.rationale: Makes the contextual destination of heart-highways readable while noting the compressed Hebrew.
verses.before: Happy are those whose strength is in you, in whose heart are the highways.
verses.after: How fortunate are those whose strength is in you, whose hearts hold the roads of pilgrimage!
verses.tsw_comparator: Happy are those whose strength is in you, in whose heart are the highways.

verses.rationale: Keeps Baca untranslated, rain and blessings, with alternative meanings noted.
verses.before: Passing through the Valley of Baca, they make it a place of springs; the early rain also covers it with blessings.
verses.after: As they pass through the Valley of Baca, they make it a place of springs; the early rain clothes it with blessings.
verses.tsw_comparator: Passing through the Valley of Baca, they make it a place of springs; the early rain also covers it with blessings.

verses.rationale: Preserves progressive strength and the individual appearance within the group.
verses.before: They go from strength to strength; each appears before God in Zion.
verses.after: They go from strength to strength; each appears before God in Zion.
verses.tsw_comparator: They go from strength to strength; each appears before God in Zion.

verses.rationale: Retains both divine titles and singular prayer.
verses.before: O LORD God of Hosts, hear my prayer; give ear, O God of Jacob. Selah.
verses.after: LORD, God of Armies, hear my prayer; listen, God of Jacob. Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: O LORD God of Hosts, hear my prayer; give ear, O God of Jacob. Selah.

verses.rationale: Reads shield parallel to anointed ruler, with the divine-shield alternative noted.
verses.before: Look upon our shield, O God; look upon the face of your anointed.
verses.after: God, look on our shield; look upon the face of your anointed one.
