verses.tsw_comparator: Look upon our shield, O God; look upon the face of your anointed.

verses.rationale: Retains exact thousand and threshold without inventing an official doorkeeper position.
verses.before: For one day in your courts is better than a thousand elsewhere. I would rather stand at the threshold of the house of my God than dwell in the tents of wickedness.
verses.after: One day in your courts is better than a thousand. I would rather stand at the threshold of my God's house than live in the tents of wickedness.
verses.tsw_comparator: For one day in your courts is better than a thousand elsewhere. I would rather stand at the threshold of the house of my God than dwell in the tents of wickedness.

verses.rationale: Preserves sun, shield, gifts and moral qualification.
verses.before: For the LORD God is sun and shield; the LORD gives grace and glory. No good thing does God withhold from people who walk with integrity.
verses.after: For the LORD God is a sun and a shield; the LORD gives favor and honor. He holds back nothing good from those who walk with integrity.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the LORD God is sun and shield; the LORD gives grace and glory. No good thing does God withhold from those who walk with integrity.

verses.rationale: Closes with the third beatitude and personal trust.
verses.before: O LORD of Hosts, happy is the one who trusts in you.
verses.after: LORD of Armies, how fortunate is the one who trusts in you!
verses.tsw_comparator: O LORD of Hosts, happy is the one who trusts in you.

verses.rationale: Follows the restoration idiom while retaining its possible captivity association in a note.
verses.before: LORD, you were favorable to your land; you restored the fortunes of Jacob.
verses.after: For the music leader. Of the sons of Korah. A psalm. LORD, you showed favor to your land; you restored Jacob's fortunes.
verses.tsw_comparator: LORD, you were favorable to your land; you restored the fortunes of Jacob.

verses.rationale: Keeps lifting and covering as distinct forgiveness images.
verses.before: You forgave the iniquity of your people; you covered all their sin. Selah.
verses.after: You lifted away your people's guilt; you covered all their sin. Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: You forgave the iniquity of your people; you covered all their sin. Selah.

verses.rationale: Retains total withdrawal and burning anger.
verses.before: You withdrew all your wrath; you turned from your burning anger.
verses.after: You withdrew all your fury and turned away from your burning anger.
verses.tsw_comparator: You withdrew all your wrath; you turned from your burning anger.

verses.rationale: Keeps the move from remembered restoration to present need.
verses.before: Restore us again, O God of our salvation, and put away your indignation toward us!
verses.after: Restore us, God our savior; put an end to your anger toward us.
verses.tsw_comparator: Restore us again, O God of our salvation, and put away your indignation toward us!

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated question across generations.
verses.before: Will you be angry with us forever? Will you prolong your anger to all generations?
verses.after: Will you be angry with us forever? Will your anger stretch from generation to generation?
verses.tsw_comparator: Will you be angry with us forever? Will you prolong your anger to all generations?

verses.rationale: Retains revived life as the ground of joy.
verses.before: Will you not revive us again, that your people may rejoice in you?
verses.after: Will you not give us life again, so your people can rejoice in you?
verses.tsw_comparator: Will you not revive us again, that your people may rejoice in you?

verses.rationale: Keeps paired love and rescue petitions.
verses.before: Show us your steadfast love, O LORD, and grant us your salvation.
verses.after: Show us your faithful love, LORD; grant us your salvation.
verses.tsw_comparator: Show us your steadfast love, O LORD, and grant us your salvation.

verses.rationale: Preserves the singular listening voice and the condition on promised peace.
verses.before: Let me hear what God the LORD will speak, for he will speak peace to his people, to his holy ones— but let them not turn back to folly.
verses.after: Let me hear what God the LORD will say. He will speak peace to his people, his faithful ones— but let them not turn back to folly.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let me hear what God the LORD will speak, for he will speak peace to his people, to his holy ones— but let them not turn back to folly.

verses.rationale: Keeps fear and indwelling glory rather than reducing glory to prosperity.
verses.before: Surely his salvation is near to people who fear him, that glory may dwell in our land.
verses.after: Surely his salvation is near those who fear him, so that glory may dwell in our land.
verses.tsw_comparator: Surely his salvation is near to those who fear him, that glory may dwell in our land.

verses.rationale: Preserves the four personifications and their bodily encounter.
verses.before: Steadfast love and faithfulness meet; righteousness and peace kiss each other.
verses.after: Faithful love and faithfulness meet; righteousness and peace kiss.
verses.tsw_comparator: Steadfast love and faithfulness meet; righteousness and peace kiss each other.

verses.rationale: Keeps the earth/heaven movements of the personifications.
verses.before: Faithfulness springs up from the ground, and righteousness looks down from heaven.
verses.after: Faithfulness sprouts from the earth, and righteousness looks down from heaven.
verses.tsw_comparator: Faithfulness springs up from the ground, and righteousness looks down from heaven.

verses.rationale: Retains material harvest within the larger restoration.
verses.before: The LORD will indeed give what is good, and our land will yield its increase.
verses.after: The LORD will indeed give what is good, and our land will yield its harvest.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD will indeed give what is good, and our land will yield its increase.

verses.rationale: Reads righteousness as preparing the route; notes the difficult final clause.
verses.before: Righteousness will go before him and will make a path for his steps.
verses.after: Righteousness will walk ahead of him and make a way for his footsteps.
verses.tsw_comparator: Righteousness will go before him and will make a path for his steps.

verses.rationale: Retains the ear-inclining appeal and concrete need.
verses.before: Incline your ear, O LORD, and answer me, for I am poor and needy.
verses.after: A prayer of David. Lean down and listen, LORD; answer me, for I am poor and needy.
verses.tsw_comparator: Incline your ear, O LORD, and answer me, for I am poor and needy.

verses.rationale: Keeps the fidelity claim, servant identity and direct trust.
verses.before: Preserve my life, for I am faithful; save your servant who trusts in you—you are my God.
verses.after: Guard my life, for I am faithful to you. You are my God; save your servant who trusts in you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Preserve my life, for I am faithful; save your servant who trusts in you—you are my God.

verses.rationale: Retains Adonai as Lord and persistent calling.
verses.before: Be gracious to me, O Lord, for to you I cry all the day.
verses.after: Be gracious to me, Lord, for I call to you all day long.
verses.tsw_comparator: Be gracious to me, O Lord, for to you I cry all the day.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated nephesh connection and lifting image.
verses.before: Gladden the soul of your servant, for to you, O Lord, I lift up my soul.
verses.after: Bring joy to your servant's life, for I lift my life to you, Lord.
verses.tsw_comparator: Gladden the soul of your servant, for to you, O Lord, I lift up my soul.

verses.rationale: Retains forgiveness and universal scope of the invitation.
verses.before: For you, O Lord, are good and forgiving, abounding in steadfast love to everyone who call upon you.
verses.after: For you, Lord, are good and ready to forgive, rich in faithful love toward everyone who calls to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you, O Lord, are good and forgiving, abounding in steadfast love to all who call upon you.

verses.rationale: Preserves the doubled hearing request.
verses.before: Give ear, O LORD, to my prayer; listen to the voice of my pleas.
verses.after: LORD, listen to my prayer; pay attention to my pleas for mercy.
verses.tsw_comparator: Give ear, O LORD, to my prayer; listen to the voice of my pleas.

verses.rationale: Keeps confident answer as the reason for prayer.
verses.before: In the day of my trouble I call upon you, for you answer me.
verses.after: When distress comes, I call to you, because you answer me.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the day of my trouble I call upon you, for you answer me.

verses.rationale: Preserves the comparison among gods without doctrinal replacement.
verses.before: There is none like you among the gods, O Lord, nor are there any works like yours.
verses.after: Among the gods there is none like you, Lord; no deeds compare with yours.
verses.tsw_comparator: There is none like you among the gods, O Lord, nor are there any works like yours.

verses.rationale: Keeps nations as created communities and their worship.
verses.before: All nations you have made will come and bow down before you, O Lord, and will glorify your name.
verses.after: All the nations you made will come and bow before you, Lord; they will honor your name.
verses.tsw_comparator: All nations you have made shall come and bow down before you, O Lord, and shall glorify your name.

verses.rationale: Retains the exclusive declaration alongside verse 8's comparison.
verses.before: For you are great and do wondrous things; you alone are God.
verses.after: For you are great and work wonders; you alone are God.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you are great and do wondrous things; you alone are God.

verses.rationale: Keeps way, walking, truth and united-heart petition.
verses.before: Teach me your way, O LORD, that I may walk in your truth; unite my heart to fear your name.
verses.after: Teach me your way, LORD, so I may walk in your truth. Give me an undivided heart to fear your name.
verses.tsw_comparator: Teach me your way, O LORD, that I may walk in your truth; unite my heart to fear your name.

verses.rationale: Connects whole-heart praise to the preceding petition.
verses.before: I give thanks to you, O Lord my God, with my whole heart, and I will glorify your name forever.
verses.after: Lord my God, I will thank you with all my heart and honor your name forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: I give thanks to you, O Lord my God, with my whole heart, and I will glorify your name forever.

verses.rationale: Retains Sheol without equating it with final punishment.
verses.before: For great is your steadfast love toward me; you have delivered my soul from the depths of Sheol.
verses.after: For your faithful love toward me is great; you have rescued my life from the depths of Sheol.
verses.tsw_comparator: For great is your steadfast love toward me; you have delivered my soul from the depths of Sheol.

verses.rationale: Keeps collective deadly hostility and neglect of God.
verses.before: O God, the arrogant have risen against me; a band of ruthless men seeks my life, and they do not set you before them.
verses.after: God, arrogant people have risen against me; a gang of ruthless men is seeking my life. They give no thought to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: O God, the arrogant have risen against me; a band of ruthless men seeks my life, and they do not set you before them.

verses.rationale: Preserves the recognizable mercy formula and both faithfulness terms.
verses.before: But you, O Lord, are a God merciful and gracious, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love and faithfulness.
verses.after: But you, Lord, are a compassionate and gracious God, slow to anger and rich in faithful love and faithfulness.
verses.tsw_comparator: But you, O Lord, are a God merciful and gracious, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love and faithfulness.

verses.rationale: Keeps the maternal servant relationship rather than removing its social language.
verses.before: Turn to me and be gracious to me; give your strength to your servant, and save the son of your maidservant.
verses.after: Turn toward me and be gracious. Give your strength to your servant; save the son of your servant woman.
verses.tsw_comparator: Turn to me and be gracious to me; give your strength to your servant, and save the son of your maidservant.

verses.rationale: Retains visible sign, opponents' shame and concluding assurance.
verses.before: Show me a sign of your favor, that people who hate me may see and be put to shame, because you, LORD, have helped me and comforted me.
verses.after: Show me a sign of your goodness, so those who hate me may see it and be ashamed, because you, LORD, have helped and comforted me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Show me a sign of your favor, that those who hate me may see and be put to shame, because you, LORD, have helped me and comforted me.

verses.rationale: Makes the founded city explicit from the Zion context while retaining its holy-mountain setting.
verses.before: God’s foundation is in the holy mountains.
verses.after: Of the sons of Korah. A psalm. A song. The city he founded stands on the holy mountains.
verses.tsw_comparator: God’s foundation is in the holy mountains.

verses.rationale: Keeps the explicit comparison and city gates.
verses.before: The LORD loves the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob.
verses.after: The LORD loves Zion's gates more than all the dwellings of Jacob.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD loves the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob.

verses.rationale: Retains the direct address to the city.
verses.before: Glorious things are spoken of you, O city of God. Selah.
verses.after: Glorious things are spoken of you, city of God. Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Glorious things are spoken of you, O city of God. Selah.

verses.rationale: Keeps all nations, divine voice and ambiguous there; explains Rahab in note.
verses.before: “I will mention Rahab and Babylon among people who know me; look—Philistia and Tyre, with Cush: ‘This one was born there.’”
verses.after: “I count Rahab and Babylon among those who know me. Look: Philistia, Tyre and Cush— ‘This one was born there.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: “I will mention Rahab and Babylon among those who know me; look—Philistia and Tyre, with Cush: ‘This one was born there.’”

verses.rationale: Retains individual inclusion and the city's feminine personification.
verses.before: And of Zion it will be said, “One and another were born in her,” for the Most High will establish her.
verses.after: Of Zion it will be said, “This one and that one were born in her,” and the Most High himself will establish her.
verses.tsw_comparator: And of Zion it will be said, “One and another were born in her,” for the Most High will establish her.

verses.rationale: Keeps the birth-register image and repeated wording.
verses.before: The LORD records, when registering the peoples, “This one was born there.” Selah.
verses.after: When the LORD records the peoples, he counts, “This one was born there.” Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD records, when registering the peoples, “This one was born there.” Selah.

verses.rationale: Preserves springs rather than reducing the image to happiness; notes possible pipers.
verses.before: Singers and dancers alike say, “All my springs are in you.”
verses.after: Singers and dancers say, “All my springs are in you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Singers and dancers alike say, “All my springs are in you.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the full difficult title and the day/night prayer sequence.
verses.before: O LORD, God of my salvation, by day I cry out; by night I am before you.
verses.after: A song. A psalm of the sons of Korah. For the music leader. According to Mahalath Leannoth. A maskil of Heman the Ezrahite. LORD, God of my salvation, I cry out by day and stand before you at night.
verses.tsw_comparator: O LORD, God of my salvation, by day I cry out; by night I am before you.

verses.rationale: Keeps approach and hearing petitions.
verses.before: Let my prayer come before you; incline your ear to my cry.
verses.after: Let my prayer come before you; lean down and hear my cry.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let my prayer come before you; incline your ear to my cry.

verses.rationale: Retains saturation with trouble and the named realm of death.
verses.before: For my soul is full of troubles, and my life draws near to Sheol.
verses.after: My life is filled with troubles; I have come to the edge of Sheol.
verses.tsw_comparator: For my soul is full of troubles, and my life draws near to Sheol.

verses.rationale: Keeps the social reckoning among the dying.
verses.before: I am counted among people who go down to the Pit; I am like one without strength,
verses.after: I am counted among those going down to the pit; I am like a man with no strength left.
verses.tsw_comparator: I am counted among those who go down to the Pit; I am like one without strength,

verses.rationale: Preserves the anguished claim of divine forgetting and ambiguous freedom/separation among the dead.
verses.before: abandoned among the dead, like the slain who lie in the grave, whom you remember no more, for they are cut off from your hand.
verses.after: I am set apart among the dead, like the slain lying in a grave, whom you remember no more, cut off from your hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: abandoned among the dead, like the slain who lie in the grave, whom you remember no more, for they are cut off from your hand.

verses.rationale: Retains explicit divine agency and layered descent.
verses.before: You have put me in the lowest pit, in dark places, in the depths.
verses.after: You have put me in the lowest pit, in dark places, in the depths.
verses.tsw_comparator: You have put me in the lowest pit, in dark places, in the depths.

verses.rationale: Keeps pressure and sea-wave images.
verses.before: Your wrath lies heavy upon me, and with all your waves you overwhelm me. Selah.
verses.after: Your fury presses heavily on me; you overwhelm me with all your breakers. Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your wrath lies heavy upon me, and with all your waves you overwhelm me. Selah.

verses.rationale: Preserves social rejection, revulsion and confinement.
verses.before: You have put my companions far from me; you have made me an abomination to them. I am shut in and cannot escape.
verses.after: You have driven my companions far away and made me repulsive to them. I am shut in, with no way out.
verses.tsw_comparator: You have put my companions far from me; you have made me an abomination to them. I am shut in and cannot escape.

verses.rationale: Keeps bodily decline and persistent prayer gesture.
verses.before: My eye wastes away because of affliction. I call to you, O LORD, every day; I spread out my hands to you.
verses.after: My eyes waste away with affliction. Every day I call to you, LORD; I spread my hands toward you.
verses.tsw_comparator: My eye wastes away because of affliction. I call to you, O LORD, every day; I spread out my hands to you.

verses.rationale: Retains shades and unanswered questions rather than inserting later resurrection conclusions.
verses.before: Do you work wonders for the dead? Do the shades rise up to praise you? Selah.
verses.after: Do you work wonders for the dead? Do the shades rise up and thank you? Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do you work wonders for the dead? Do the shades rise up to praise you? Selah.

verses.rationale: Keeps grave and Abaddon as paired death-world terms.
verses.before: Is your steadfast love declared in the grave, or your faithfulness in Abaddon?
verses.after: Is your faithful love recounted in the grave, your faithfulness in Abaddon?
verses.tsw_comparator: Is your steadfast love declared in the grave, or your faithfulness in Abaddon?

verses.rationale: Preserves the location of forgetting and the repeated question structure.
verses.before: Are your wonders known in the darkness, or your righteousness in the land of forgetfulness?
verses.after: Are your wonders known in the darkness, your righteousness in the land of oblivion?
verses.tsw_comparator: Are your wonders known in the darkness, or your righteousness in the land of forgetfulness?

verses.rationale: Keeps the persistent turn despite absent relief.
verses.before: Yet I, O LORD, cry to you; in the morning my prayer comes before you.
verses.after: But I cry to you for help, LORD; in the morning my prayer comes to meet you.
verses.tsw_comparator: But I, O LORD, cry to you; in the morning my prayer comes before you.

verses.rationale: Retains the direct questions without adding reassurance.
verses.before: Why, O LORD, do you reject my soul? Why do you hide your face from me?
verses.after: Why, LORD, do you reject me? Why do you hide your face from me?
verses.tsw_comparator: Why, O LORD, do you reject my soul? Why do you hide your face from me?

verses.rationale: Keeps lifelong suffering; notes the rare final verb's uncertainty.
verses.before: Afflicted and near death from my youth, I bear your terrors; I am helpless.
verses.after: From my youth I have been afflicted and near death; I bear your terrors and am overwhelmed.
verses.tsw_comparator: Afflicted and near death from my youth, I bear your terrors; I am helpless.

verses.rationale: Preserves the speaker's extreme claim and divine possessives.
verses.before: Your burning wrath has swept over me; your terrors have destroyed me.
verses.after: Your burning anger has swept over me; your terrors have destroyed me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your burning wrath has swept over me; your terrors have destroyed me.

verses.rationale: Retains surrounding flood as the action of terrors.
verses.before: They surround me like water all day long; they close in on me together.
verses.after: All day they surround me like water; they close in on me from every side.
verses.tsw_comparator: They surround me like water all day long; they close in on me together.

verses.rationale: Keeps the abrupt final darkness without supplying a hopeful ending.
verses.before: You have put friend and neighbor far from me; my companions are darkness.
verses.after: You have driven lover and friend far from me; my companions are darkness.
verses.tsw_comparator: You have put friend and neighbor far from me; my companions are darkness.

verses.rationale: Preserves title, lasting love and direct-address transition.
verses.before: I will sing of the steadfast love of the LORD forever; with my mouth I will reveal your faithfulness to all generations.
verses.after: A maskil of Ethan the Ezrahite. I will sing of the LORD's faithful love forever; with my mouth I will make your faithfulness known to every generation.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will sing of the steadfast love of the LORD forever; with my mouth I will make known your faithfulness to all generations.

verses.rationale: Keeps I said as pinned and the building image.
verses.before: For I said, “Steadfast love will be built up forever; in the heavens you will establish your faithfulness.”
verses.after: For I said, “Faithful love is built to last forever; you establish your faithfulness in the heavens.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For I said, “Steadfast love will be built up forever; in the heavens you will establish your faithfulness.”

verses.rationale: Marks the divine voice and both covenant and oath.
verses.before: You said, “I have made a covenant with my chosen one; I have sworn to David my servant:
verses.after: “I have made a covenant with my chosen one; I have sworn to David my servant:
verses.tsw_comparator: You said, “I have made a covenant with my chosen one; I have sworn to David my servant:

verses.rationale: Preserves dynastic offspring and throne-building repetition.
verses.before: ‘I will establish your offspring forever, and build your throne for all generations.’” Selah.
verses.after: ‘I will establish your offspring forever and build your throne for every generation.’” Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: ‘I will establish your offspring forever, and build your throne for all generations.’” Selah.

verses.rationale: Keeps the heavenly assembly and faithfulness theme.
verses.before: Let the heavens praise your wonders, O LORD, your faithfulness in the assembly of the holy ones!
verses.after: The heavens praise your wonders, LORD, your faithfulness in the assembly of holy ones.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let the heavens praise your wonders, O LORD, your faithfulness in the assembly of the holy ones!

verses.rationale: Retains the unusual divine-sons designation and both occurrences of the name.
verses.before: For who in the skies can be compared to the LORD? Who among the sons of God is like the LORD,
verses.after: Who in the skies can compare with the LORD? Who among the sons of gods is like the LORD?
verses.tsw_comparator: For who in the skies can be compared to the LORD? Who among the sons of God is like the LORD,

verses.rationale: Keeps divine council imagery and comparative awe.
verses.before: a God greatly feared in the council of the holy ones, and awesome above everyone who are around him?
verses.after: God is greatly feared in the council of holy ones, more awesome than all who surround him.
verses.tsw_comparator: a God greatly feared in the council of the holy ones, and awesome above all who are around him?

verses.rationale: Preserves both full and short divine names and surrounding faithfulness.
verses.before: O LORD God of hosts, who is mighty like you, O LORD, with your faithfulness all around you?
verses.after: LORD, God of Armies, who is mighty like you, YAH? Your faithfulness surrounds you.
verses.tsw_comparator: O LORD God of hosts, who is mighty like you, O LORD, with your faithfulness all around you?

verses.rationale: Keeps pride/raging sense and calming action.
verses.before: You rule the raging of the sea; when its waves rise, you still them.
verses.after: You rule the sea's raging pride; when its waves rise, you still them.
verses.tsw_comparator: You rule the raging of the sea; when its waves rise, you still them.

verses.rationale: Retains mythic Rahab and the slain comparison, with an explanatory note.
verses.before: You crushed Rahab like a carcass; you scattered your enemies with your mighty arm.
verses.after: You crushed Rahab like a slain warrior; with your strong arm you scattered your enemies.
verses.tsw_comparator: You crushed Rahab like a carcass; you scattered your enemies with your mighty arm.

verses.rationale: Preserves ownership and founding as distinct assertions.
verses.before: The heavens are yours; the earth also is yours; the world and all that is in it—you have founded them.
verses.after: The heavens are yours; the earth is yours too. You founded the world and everything in it.
verses.tsw_comparator: The heavens are yours; the earth also is yours; the world and all that is in it—you have founded them.

verses.rationale: Keeps directions and both named mountains.
verses.before: The north and the south—you have created them; Tabor and Hermon shout for joy at your name.
verses.after: You created north and south; Tabor and Hermon shout for joy at your name.
verses.tsw_comparator: The north and the south—you have created them; Tabor and Hermon shout for joy at your name.

verses.rationale: Retains the three-part bodily power imagery.
verses.before: You have a mighty arm; strong is your hand, high your right hand.
verses.after: Your arm is mighty; your hand is strong, your right hand raised high.
verses.tsw_comparator: You have a mighty arm; strong is your hand, high your right hand.

verses.rationale: Preserves all four qualities as structural and processional images.
verses.before: Righteousness and justice are the foundation of your throne; steadfast love and faithfulness go before you.
verses.after: Righteousness and justice are your throne's foundation; faithful love and faithfulness go before you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Righteousness and justice are the foundation of your throne; steadfast love and faithfulness go before you.

verses.rationale: Keeps festival acclamation and face-light walking.
verses.before: Blessed are the people who know the festal shout, who walk, O LORD, in the light of your face,
verses.after: How fortunate are the people who know the shout of celebration! LORD, they walk in the light of your face.
verses.tsw_comparator: Blessed are the people who know the festal shout, who walk, O LORD, in the light of your face,

verses.rationale: Retains the sustained joy and raising action.
verses.before: who rejoice in your name all the day and in your righteousness are exalted.
verses.after: They rejoice in your name all day long and are lifted high by your righteousness.
verses.tsw_comparator: who rejoice in your name all the day and in your righteousness are exalted.

verses.rationale: Follows qere passive rise and preserves their/our shift and horn.
verses.before: For you are the glory of their strength; by your favor our horn is exalted.
verses.after: For you are the splendor of their strength; by your favor our horn is lifted high.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you are the glory of their strength; by your favor our horn is exalted.

verses.rationale: Keeps the king parallel explaining the shield metaphor.
verses.before: For our shield belongs to the LORD, our king to the Holy One of Israel.
verses.after: Our shield belongs to the LORD, our king to the Holy One of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: For our shield belongs to the LORD, our king to the Holy One of Israel.

verses.rationale: Retains plural faithful ones in the pinned text and the divine announcement.
verses.before: Of old you spoke in a vision to your faithful one and said: “I have granted help to one who is mighty; I have exalted one chosen from the people.
verses.after: Then you spoke in a vision to your faithful ones: “I have given help to a warrior; I have raised up a chosen man from the people.
verses.tsw_comparator: Of old you spoke in a vision to your faithful one and said: “I have granted help to one who is mighty; I have exalted one chosen from the people.

verses.rationale: Keeps finding and anointing with concrete oil.
verses.before: I have found David my servant; with my holy oil I have anointed him,
verses.after: I have found David my servant; I have anointed him with my holy oil.
verses.tsw_comparator: I have found David my servant; with my holy oil I have anointed him,

verses.rationale: Preserves hand and arm as separate parallel clauses.
verses.before: so that my hand will be established with him; my arm also will strengthen him.
verses.after: My hand will remain firm with him; my arm will strengthen him.
verses.tsw_comparator: so that my hand shall be established with him; my arm also shall strengthen him.

verses.rationale: Chooses the creditor/oppressor sense of yashi while noting outwitting as an alternative.
verses.before: The enemy will not outwit him; the wicked will not humble him.
verses.after: No enemy will exact tribute from him; no wicked man will oppress him.
verses.tsw_comparator: The enemy shall not outwit him; the wicked shall not humble him.

verses.rationale: Keeps the explicit violence of the royal promise.
verses.before: I will crush his foes before him and strike down people who hate him.
verses.after: I will crush his foes before him and strike down those who hate him.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will crush his foes before him and strike down those who hate him.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated covenant attributes and horn image.
verses.before: My faithfulness and my steadfast love will be with him, and in my name his horn will be exalted.
verses.after: My faithfulness and faithful love will be with him; through my name his horn will be lifted high.
verses.tsw_comparator: My faithfulness and my steadfast love shall be with him, and in my name his horn shall be exalted.

verses.rationale: Retains geographical scope through bodily imagery without adding borders.
verses.before: I will set his hand on the sea and his right hand on the rivers.
verses.after: I will set his hand over the sea, his right hand over the rivers.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will set his hand on the sea and his right hand on the rivers.

verses.rationale: Keeps royal sonship and rock title together.
verses.before: He will cry to me, ‘You are my Father, my God, and the Rock of my salvation.’
verses.after: He will call to me, ‘You are my father, my God, the rock of my salvation.’
verses.tsw_comparator: He shall cry to me, ‘You are my Father, my God, and the Rock of my salvation.’

verses.rationale: Retains bestowed rank rather than suggesting biological birth order.
verses.before: I will make him the firstborn, the highest of the kings of the earth.
verses.after: I will make him my firstborn, the highest of the kings of the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: And I will make him the firstborn, the highest of the kings of the earth.

verses.rationale: Follows qere keep with enduring covenant assurance.
verses.before: My steadfast love I will keep for him forever, and my covenant will stand firm for him.
verses.after: I will keep my faithful love for him forever; my covenant with him will stand firm.
verses.tsw_comparator: My steadfast love I will keep for him forever, and my covenant will stand firm for him.

verses.rationale: Keeps offspring and throne with cosmic duration.
verses.before: I will establish his offspring forever and his throne as the days of the heavens.
verses.after: I will establish his offspring for all time, his throne as long as the heavens endure.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will establish his offspring forever and his throne as the days of the heavens.

verses.rationale: Retains specific royal sons and conditional structure.
verses.before: If his children forsake my law and do not walk according to my rules,
verses.after: If his sons abandon my instruction and do not walk by my rulings,
verses.tsw_comparator: If his children forsake my law and do not walk according to my rules,

verses.rationale: Preserves the second conditional pair rather than compressing repetition.
verses.before: if they violate my statutes and do not keep my commandments,
verses.after: if they profane my statutes and do not keep my commands,
verses.tsw_comparator: if they violate my statutes and do not keep my commandments,

verses.rationale: Keeps corporeal punishment and moral distinctions.
verses.before: then I will punish their transgression with the rod and their iniquity with stripes,
verses.after: I will punish their rebellion with a rod and their wrongdoing with blows.
verses.tsw_comparator: then I will punish their transgression with the rod and their iniquity with stripes,

verses.rationale: Retains the shift from sons to him and the covenant limitation on punishment.
verses.before: but I will not remove from him my steadfast love or be false to my faithfulness.
verses.after: But I will not withdraw my faithful love from him or betray my faithfulness.
verses.tsw_comparator: but I will not remove from him my steadfast love or be false to my faithfulness.

verses.rationale: Preserves profanation echo and spoken commitment.
verses.before: I will not violate my covenant or alter the word that went forth from my lips.
verses.after: I will not profane my covenant or change what my lips have spoken.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will not violate my covenant or alter the word that went forth from my lips.

verses.rationale: Renders the Hebrew oath idiom as a firm negative, not a conditional possibility.
verses.before: Once for all I have sworn by my holiness; I will not lie to David.
verses.after: Once for all I have sworn by my holiness; I will not lie to David.
verses.tsw_comparator: Once for all I have sworn by my holiness; I will not lie to David.

verses.rationale: Keeps solar comparison and divine presence.
verses.before: His offspring will endure forever, his throne as long as the sun before me.
verses.after: His offspring will last forever, and his throne will be like the sun before me.
verses.tsw_comparator: His offspring shall endure forever, his throne as long as the sun before me.

verses.rationale: Preserves lunar witness imagery, noting the witness's possible distinct identity.
verses.before: Like the moon it will be established forever, a faithful witness in the skies.” Selah.
verses.after: Like the moon it will be established forever, a faithful witness in the skies.” Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Like the moon it shall be established forever, a faithful witness in the skies.” Selah.

verses.rationale: Keeps the sharp protest against the preceding promise.
verses.before: But now you have cast off and rejected; you are full of wrath against your anointed.
verses.after: But you have rejected and spurned him; you have been furious with your anointed one.
verses.tsw_comparator: But now you have cast off and rejected; you are full of wrath against your anointed.

verses.rationale: Retains the accusation of covenant repudiation without explaining it away.
verses.before: You have renounced the covenant with your servant; you have defiled his crown in the dust.
verses.after: You have renounced your servant's covenant; you have defiled his crown in the dust.
verses.tsw_comparator: You have renounced the covenant with your servant; you have defiled his crown in the dust.

verses.rationale: Keeps defensive structures and total damage.
verses.before: You have breached all his walls; you have laid his strongholds in ruins.
verses.after: You have broken down all his walls and reduced his fortresses to ruins.
verses.tsw_comparator: You have breached all his walls; you have laid his strongholds in ruins.

verses.rationale: Retains ongoing vulnerability and local contempt.
verses.before: Everyone who pass by plunder him; he has become a reproach to his neighbors.
verses.after: Everyone passing by plunders him; he has become a disgrace to his neighbors.
verses.tsw_comparator: All who pass by plunder him; he has become a reproach to his neighbors.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine agency in the enemy's advantage.
verses.before: You have exalted the right hand of his foes; you have made all his enemies rejoice.
verses.after: You have raised his enemies' right hand and made all his foes rejoice.
verses.tsw_comparator: You have exalted the right hand of his foes; you have made all his enemies rejoice.

verses.rationale: Preserves military defeat and withheld support.
verses.before: You have turned back the edge of his sword and have not made him stand in battle.
verses.after: You have turned back the edge of his sword and have not sustained him in battle.
verses.tsw_comparator: You have turned back the edge of his sword and have not made him stand in battle.

verses.rationale: Chooses splendor for the difficult purity/brightness term with a note.
verses.before: You have put an end to his splendor and cast his throne to the ground.
verses.after: You have put an end to his splendor and hurled his throne to the ground.
verses.tsw_comparator: You have put an end to his splendor and cast his throne to the ground.

verses.rationale: Retains shortened youth and shame as a garment.
verses.before: You have shortened the days of his youth; you have covered him with shame. Selah.
verses.after: You have cut short the days of his youth and wrapped him in shame. Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: You have shortened the days of his youth; you have covered him with shame. Selah.

verses.rationale: Preserves unanswered duration questions and fire image.
verses.before: How long, O LORD? Will you hide yourself forever? Will your wrath burn like fire?
verses.after: How long, LORD? Will you hide forever? Will your fury keep burning like fire?
verses.tsw_comparator: How long, O LORD? Will you hide yourself forever? Will your wrath burn like fire?

verses.rationale: Keeps first-person mortality and the searching creation question.
verses.before: Remember how short my time is! For what vanity you have created all the children of humanity!
verses.after: Remember how brief my life is. Why have you created all human beings for such futility?
verses.tsw_comparator: Remember how short my time is! For what vanity you have created all the children of humanity!

verses.rationale: Retains death sight and Sheol's grasp as distinct images.
verses.before: What man can live and never see death? Who can deliver his soul from the power of Sheol? Selah.
verses.after: What man can live without seeing death? Who can rescue his life from the hand of Sheol? Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: What man can live and never see death? Who can deliver his soul from the power of Sheol? Selah.

verses.rationale: Keeps the concluding appeal to oath and past love.
verses.before: Lord, where is your former steadfast love, which by your faithfulness you swore to David?
verses.after: Lord, where is your former faithful love, which in your faithfulness you swore to David?
verses.tsw_comparator: Lord, where is your former steadfast love, which by your faithfulness you swore to David?

verses.rationale: Renders the compressed final clause with implied taunts from the context; marks the difficulty.
verses.before: Remember, O Lord, how your servants are mocked, and how I bear in my heart the insults of all the many nations,
verses.after: Remember, Lord, the disgrace your servants bear, how I carry in my breast the taunts of all the many peoples,
verses.tsw_comparator: Remember, O Lord, how your servants are mocked, and how I bear in my heart the insults of all the many nations,

verses.rationale: Retains footsteps rather than rewriting them as delayed messianic arrival.
verses.before: with which your enemies mock, O LORD, with which they mock the footsteps of your anointed.
verses.after: the taunts of your enemies, LORD, who mock every step of your anointed one.
verses.tsw_comparator: with which your enemies mock, O LORD, with which they mock the footsteps of your anointed.

verses.rationale: Preserves the book-closing doxology and doubled amen amid unresolved lament.
verses.before: Blessed be the LORD forever! Amen and Amen.
verses.after: Blessed be the LORD forever. Amen and amen.
verses.tsw_comparator: Blessed be the LORD forever! Amen and Amen.

verses.rationale: Retains title attribution and home image across generations.
verses.before: Lord, you have been our dwelling place in all generations.
verses.after: A prayer of Moses, the man of God. Lord, you have been our dwelling place from generation to generation.
verses.tsw_comparator: Lord, you have been our dwelling place in all generations.

verses.rationale: Preserves the birth imagery and God's unbounded duration.
verses.before: Before the mountains were born, or you brought forth the earth and the world, from everlasting to everlasting you are God.
verses.after: Before the mountains were born, before you brought forth the earth and the world, from eternity to eternity, you are God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Before the mountains were born, or you brought forth the earth and the world, from everlasting to everlasting you are God.

verses.rationale: Renders crushed material as dust with a note and preserves the double return.
verses.before: You return humanity to dust and say, “Return, children of Adam.”
verses.after: You turn human beings back to dust and say, “Return, children of humanity.”
verses.tsw_comparator: You return humanity to dust and say, “Return, children of Adam.”

verses.rationale: Keeps exact thousand and both time comparisons without conversion formulas.
verses.before: For a thousand years in your sight are like yesterday when it passes, or like a watch in the night.
verses.after: A thousand years in your sight are like yesterday once it has passed, like a watch in the night.
verses.tsw_comparator: For a thousand years in your sight are like yesterday when it passes, or like a watch in the night.

verses.rationale: Preserves flooding away, sleep and fresh grass images.
verses.before: You sweep them away—they are like a dream, like grass that is renewed in the morning:
verses.after: You sweep them away; they are like sleep, like grass that springs up in the morning.
verses.tsw_comparator: You sweep them away—they are like a dream, like grass that is renewed in the morning:

verses.rationale: Keeps the day-length contrast and both final decay verbs.
verses.before: in the morning it flourishes and is renewed; in the evening it fades and withers.
verses.after: In the morning it blooms and grows; by evening it withers and dries up.
verses.tsw_comparator: in the morning it flourishes and is renewed; in the evening it fades and withers.

verses.rationale: Retains the communal confession under divine anger.
verses.before: For we are brought to an end by your anger; by your wrath we are dismayed.
verses.after: Your anger consumes us; your fury leaves us terrified.
verses.tsw_comparator: For we are brought to an end by your anger; by your wrath we are dismayed.

verses.rationale: Follows qere set; keeps illumination of what is hidden.
verses.before: You have set our iniquities before you, our hidden sins in the light of your presence.
verses.after: You have set our wrongs before you, our hidden sins in the light of your face.
verses.tsw_comparator: You have set our iniquities before you, our hidden sins in the light of your presence.

verses.rationale: Preserves lifespan and sigh rather than a developed-life narrative.
verses.before: For all our days pass away under your wrath; we bring our years to an end like a sigh.
verses.after: All our days pass under your wrath; we finish our years like a sigh.
verses.tsw_comparator: For all our days pass away under your wrath; we bring our years to an end like a sigh.

verses.rationale: Keeps exact ages, limited strength and the flight image.
verses.before: The years of our life are seventy, or even by strength eighty; yet their span is toil and trouble; they are soon gone, and we fly away.
verses.after: Our years amount to seventy, or eighty if we have the strength. Yet all they boast of is toil and sorrow; they pass quickly, and we fly away.
verses.tsw_comparator: The years of our life are seventy, or even by strength eighty; yet their span is toil and trouble; they are soon gone, and we fly away.

verses.rationale: Retains the difficult relation between wrath and fear without redefining fear as mere respect.
verses.before: Who considers the power of your anger, and your wrath according to the fear of you?
verses.after: Who understands the strength of your anger, your fury in keeping with the fear you deserve?
verses.tsw_comparator: Who considers the power of your anger, and your wrath according to the fear of you?

verses.rationale: Keeps counting as the route to wise-hearted living.
verses.before: So teach us to number our days, that we may gain a heart of wisdom.
verses.after: Teach us to count our days rightly, so we may gain a heart of wisdom.
verses.tsw_comparator: So teach us to number our days, that we may gain a heart of wisdom.

verses.rationale: Preserves the reversal of return language and urgent unfinished question.
verses.before: Return, O LORD! How long? Have compassion on your servants!
verses.after: Return, LORD! How long? Have compassion on your servants.
verses.tsw_comparator: Return, O LORD! How long? Have compassion on your servants!

verses.rationale: Keeps morning answer to mortality and all-days joy.
verses.before: Satisfy us in the morning with your steadfast love, that we may rejoice and be glad all our days.
verses.after: Satisfy us in the morning with your faithful love, so we may sing for joy and be glad all our days.
verses.tsw_comparator: Satisfy us in the morning with your steadfast love, that we may rejoice and be glad all our days.

verses.rationale: Retains the proportional request and explicit divine affliction.
verses.before: Make us glad for as many days as you have afflicted us, for as many years as we have seen evil.
verses.after: Give us as many days of joy as days you afflicted us, as many years as we have known trouble.
verses.tsw_comparator: Make us glad for as many days as you have afflicted us, for as many years as we have seen evil.

verses.rationale: Keeps work and splendor with intergenerational extension.
verses.before: Let your work be shown to your servants, and your splendor to their children.
verses.after: Let your servants see your work, and their children your splendor.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let your work be shown to your servants, and your splendor to their children.

verses.rationale: Retains the deliberate full closing repetition.
verses.before: Let the favor of the Lord our God be upon us, and establish the work of our hands upon us— yes, establish the work of our hands.
verses.after: May the favor of the Lord our God rest on us. Establish the work of our hands for us— yes, establish the work of our hands.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let the favor of the Lord our God be upon us, and establish the work of our hands upon us— yes, establish the work of our hands.

verses.rationale: Keeps dwelling/night lodging and transliterated divine title.
verses.before: The one who sits in the shelter of the Most High, who lodges in the shadow of the Almighty—
verses.after: Whoever dwells in the shelter of the Most High will spend the night in Shaddai's shadow.
verses.tsw_comparator: The one who sits in the shelter of the Most High, who lodges in the shadow of the Almighty—

verses.rationale: Preserves pinned first-person I say rather than harmonizing to you say.
verses.before: I say of the LORD, “My refuge and my stronghold, my God, in whom I trust.”
verses.after: I say to the LORD, “My refuge and my fortress, my God, in whom I trust.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I say of the LORD, “My refuge and my stronghold, my God, in whom I trust.”

verses.rationale: Retains trap and disease as distinct dangers.
verses.before: For he will deliver you from the snare of the fowler, from the deadly pestilence;
verses.after: He will rescue you from the bird-catcher's snare and from deadly plague.
verses.tsw_comparator: For he will deliver you from the snare of the fowler, from the deadly pestilence;

verses.rationale: Keeps maternal bird and military protection imagery; notes rare soherah.
verses.before: he will cover you with his pinions, and under his wings you will find refuge; his faithfulness is shield and rampart.
verses.after: He will cover you with his feathers; you will find refuge beneath his wings. His faithfulness is a shield and a protective wall.
verses.tsw_comparator: he will cover you with his pinions, and under his wings you will find refuge; his faithfulness is shield and rampart.

verses.rationale: Keeps the day/night pair and continuation.
verses.before: You will not fear the terror of the night, nor the arrow that flies by day,
verses.after: You will not fear the terror of night or the arrow that flies by day,
verses.tsw_comparator: You will not fear the terror of the night, nor the arrow that flies by day,

verses.rationale: Preserves personified plague and noon devastation.
verses.before: nor the pestilence that walks in darkness, nor the destruction that lays waste at noon.
verses.after: nor the plague that walks in darkness nor the destruction that ravages at noon.
verses.tsw_comparator: nor the pestilence that walks in darkness, nor the destruction that lays waste at noon.

verses.rationale: Retains exact escalating numbers and uncompromised assurance.
verses.before: A thousand may fall at your side, and ten thousand at your right hand; it will not come near you.
verses.after: A thousand may fall beside you, ten thousand at your right hand, but it will not come near you.
verses.tsw_comparator: A thousand may fall at your side, and ten thousand at your right hand; it will not come near you.

verses.rationale: Keeps witness rather than participation in the punishment.
verses.before: You will only look with your eyes and see the recompense of the wicked.
verses.after: You will only look with your eyes and see the wicked receive their due.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will only look with your eyes and see the recompense of the wicked.

verses.rationale: Preserves the change of address instead of replacing my with your.
verses.before: Because you have made the LORD your refuge, the Most High your dwelling,
verses.after: For you, LORD, are my refuge. You have made the Most High your dwelling place;
verses.tsw_comparator: Because you have made the LORD your refuge, the Most High your dwelling,

verses.rationale: Keeps paired assurances and the concrete tent.
verses.before: no harm will befall you, no plague will come near your tent.
verses.after: no harm will meet you, no plague will come near your tent.
verses.tsw_comparator: no harm will befall you, no plague will come near your tent.

verses.rationale: Retains all your ways and angels as the commanded agents.
verses.before: For he will command his angels concerning you, to guard you in all your ways;
verses.after: For he will command his angels concerning you, to guard you in all your ways.
verses.tsw_comparator: For he will command his angels concerning you, to guard you in all your ways;

verses.rationale: Keeps hand and foot specificity.
verses.before: on their hands they will bear you up, lest you strike your foot against a stone.
verses.after: They will carry you on their hands, so you do not strike your foot against a stone.
verses.tsw_comparator: on their hands they will bear you up, lest you strike your foot against a stone.

verses.rationale: Retains four animal terms, with tannin uncertainty explained in vocabulary.
verses.before: You will tread on the lion and the cobra; the young lion and the serpent you will trample underfoot.
verses.after: You will tread on lion and cobra; you will trample young lion and serpent.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will tread on the lion and the cobra; the young lion and the serpent you will trample underfoot.

verses.rationale: Marks the divine voice and retains attachment, elevation and known name.
verses.before: “Because he holds fast to me in love, I will deliver him; I will set him on high, because he knows my name.
verses.after: “Because he clings to me in love, I will free him; I will set him safely on high, because he knows my name.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Because he holds fast to me in love, I will deliver him; I will set him on high, because he knows my name.

verses.rationale: Preserves actual distress within the psalm's strong protection claims.
verses.before: When he calls to me, I will answer him; I will be with him in trouble; I will deliver him and honor him.
verses.after: He will call to me, and I will answer. I will be with him in distress; I will rescue him and honor him.
verses.tsw_comparator: When he calls to me, I will answer him; I will be with him in trouble; I will deliver him and honor him.

verses.rationale: Keeps length of life and experienced salvation without adding immortality.
verses.before: With long life I will satisfy him and show him my salvation.”
verses.after: I will satisfy him with a long life and let him see my salvation.”
verses.tsw_comparator: With long life I will satisfy him and show him my salvation.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the Sabbath title and shift to direct address.
verses.before: It is good to give thanks to the LORD, to sing praise to your name, Most High;
verses.after: A psalm. A song for the Sabbath day. It is good to thank the LORD and sing to your name, Most High,
verses.tsw_comparator: It is good to give thanks to the LORD, to sing praise to your name, Most High;

verses.rationale: Keeps morning and plural nights, with love/faithfulness distinction.
verses.before: to declare your steadfast love in the morning, and your faithfulness by night,
verses.after: to tell of your faithful love in the morning and your faithfulness through the nights,
verses.tsw_comparator: to declare your steadfast love in the morning, and your faithfulness by night,

verses.rationale: Preserves the instrument list while avoiding a precise unsupported musical reconstruction.
verses.before: with the ten-stringed instrument and the harp, with the melody of the lyre.
verses.after: with the ten-stringed instrument and the harp, with music resounding on the lyre.
verses.tsw_comparator: with the ten-stringed instrument and the harp, with the melody of the lyre.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine work and hands as grounds of joy.
verses.before: For you, O LORD, have made me glad by your work; at the works of your hands I sing for joy.
verses.after: For your work has made me glad, LORD; at the works of your hands I shout for joy.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you, O LORD, have made me glad by your work; at the works of your hands I sing for joy.

verses.rationale: Preserves the paired exclamations and depth image.
verses.before: How great are your works, O LORD! your thoughts are very deep.
verses.after: How great your works are, LORD! How very deep your thoughts!
verses.tsw_comparator: How great are your works, O LORD! your thoughts are very deep.

verses.rationale: Introduces the following paradox rather than treating this as a general insult.
verses.before: A dull person does not know, and a fool does not understand this:
verses.after: A senseless person does not know; a fool cannot understand this:
verses.tsw_comparator: A dull person does not know, and a fool does not understand this:

verses.rationale: Keeps apparent flourishing and its severe stated outcome.
verses.before: that though the wicked sprout like grass, and all evildoers flourish, they are doomed to destruction forever;
verses.after: though the wicked sprout like grass and all who do wrong flourish, it is only for them to be destroyed forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: that though the wicked sprout like grass, and all evildoers flourish, they are doomed to destruction forever;

verses.rationale: Retains the short central contrast.
verses.before: but you, O LORD, are on high forever.
verses.after: But you, LORD, are exalted forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: but you, O LORD, are on high forever.

verses.rationale: Preserves the emphatic repeated opening.
verses.before: For look, your enemies, O LORD, for look, your enemies will perish; all evildoers will be scattered.
verses.after: Look, your enemies, LORD— look, your enemies will perish! All who do wrong will be scattered.
verses.tsw_comparator: For behold, your enemies, O LORD, for behold, your enemies shall perish; all evildoers shall be scattered.

verses.rationale: Keeps horn, wild ox and oil; notes uncertainty in the oil verb.
verses.before: But you have exalted my horn like that of a wild ox; you have poured over me fresh oil.
verses.after: You have raised my horn like a wild ox's; I am refreshed with fresh oil.
verses.tsw_comparator: But you have exalted my horn like that of a wild ox; you have poured over me fresh oil.

verses.rationale: Leaves the seen/heard outcome implicit instead of adding rejoicing in deaths.
verses.before: My eyes have seen the downfall of my enemies; my ears have heard the doom of the evildoers who rise against me.
verses.after: My eyes have looked upon those watching for my downfall; my ears have heard about the evildoers who rise against me.
verses.tsw_comparator: My eyes have seen the downfall of my enemies; my ears have heard the doom of the evildoers who rise against me.

verses.rationale: Keeps two durable trees contrasting with wicked grass.
verses.before: The righteous flourish like the palm tree, and grow like a cedar in Lebanon.
verses.after: The righteous flourish like a palm tree and grow tall like a cedar in Lebanon.
verses.tsw_comparator: The righteous flourish like the palm tree, and grow like a cedar in Lebanon.

verses.rationale: Preserves transplantation into sacred courts.
verses.before: They are planted in the house of the LORD; they flourish in the courts of our God.
verses.after: Planted in the LORD's house, they flourish in the courts of our God.
verses.tsw_comparator: They are planted in the house of the LORD; they flourish in the courts of our God.

verses.rationale: Keeps old-age fruit and living-tree imagery.
verses.before: In old age they still bear fruit; they are full of sap and green,
verses.after: Even in old age they still bear fruit; they remain full of sap and green,
verses.tsw_comparator: In old age they still bear fruit; they are full of sap and green,

verses.rationale: Follows qere injustice and preserves the personal rock conclusion.
verses.before: to declare that the LORD is upright; he is my rock, and there is no unrighteousness in him.
verses.after: declaring, “The LORD is upright. He is my rock; there is no injustice in him.”
verses.tsw_comparator: to declare that the LORD is upright; he is my rock, and there is no unrighteousness in him.

verses.rationale: Keeps doubled clothing and the stabilized world.
verses.before: The LORD reigns; he is clothed with majesty. The LORD is clothed, he has girded himself with strength. Indeed, the world is established; it will not be moved.
verses.after: The LORD reigns, clothed in majesty; the LORD is clothed in strength and has fastened it around himself. The world stands firm; it cannot be shaken.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD reigns; he is clothed with majesty. The LORD is clothed, he has girded himself with strength. Indeed, the world is established; it shall not be moved.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes throne establishment from God's eternal existence.
verses.before: Your throne is established from of old; you are from everlasting.
verses.after: Your throne has stood firm from long ago; you are from eternity.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your throne is established from of old; you are from everlasting.

verses.rationale: Preserves the triple rivers repetition and rising sound.
verses.before: The floods have lifted up, O LORD, the floods have lifted up their voice; the floods lift up their roaring.
verses.after: The rivers have risen, LORD; the rivers have raised their voice; the rivers raise their pounding waves.
verses.tsw_comparator: The floods have lifted up, O LORD, the floods have lifted up their voice; the floods lift up their roaring.

verses.rationale: Keeps the threefold might comparison.
verses.before: More than the voices of many waters, more than the mighty breakers of the sea, the LORD on high is mighty.
verses.after: Mightier than the thunder of great waters, mightier than the breakers of the sea, the LORD on high is mighty.
verses.tsw_comparator: More than the voices of many waters, more than the mighty breakers of the sea, the LORD on high is mighty.

verses.rationale: Retains testimonies, holy dwelling and enduring time.
verses.before: Your testimonies are very sure; holiness befits your house, O LORD, for length of days.
verses.after: Your testimonies are wholly trustworthy. Holiness adorns your house, LORD, for days without end.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your testimonies are very sure; holiness befits your house, O LORD, for length of days.

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated vengeance and the appearance plea.
verses.before: O LORD, God of vengeance, God of vengeance, shine forth!
verses.after: LORD, God of vengeance, God of vengeance, shine forth!
verses.tsw_comparator: O LORD, God of vengeance, God of vengeance, shine forth!

verses.rationale: Retains worldwide judgment and recompense.
verses.before: Rise up, Judge of the earth; repay the proud what they deserve.
verses.after: Rise, judge of the earth; repay the arrogant what they deserve.
verses.tsw_comparator: Rise up, Judge of the earth; repay the proud what they deserve.

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated unresolved question.
verses.before: How long, O LORD, will the wicked— how long will the wicked exult?
verses.after: How long will the wicked, LORD— how long will the wicked triumph?
verses.tsw_comparator: How long, O LORD, will the wicked— how long will the wicked exult?

verses.rationale: Keeps flowing speech and self-exaltation.
verses.before: They pour out arrogant words; everyone who do evil boast.
verses.after: They pour out arrogant words; all who do wrong boast about themselves.
verses.tsw_comparator: They pour out arrogant words; all who do evil boast.

verses.rationale: Retains crushing violence and people-as-inheritance.
verses.before: They crush your people, O LORD, and afflict your inheritance.
verses.after: They crush your people, LORD, and afflict your inheritance.
verses.tsw_comparator: They crush your people, O LORD, and afflict your inheritance.

verses.rationale: Keeps specific vulnerable groups and actual killing.
verses.before: They kill the widow and the sojourner, and they murder the orphan.
verses.after: They kill the widow and the resident foreigner; they murder the fatherless.
verses.tsw_comparator: They kill the widow and the sojourner, and they murder the orphan.

verses.rationale: Retains the short divine name and quoted denial.
verses.before: They say, “The LORD does not see; the God of Jacob does not perceive.”
verses.after: They say, “YAH does not see; the God of Jacob pays no attention.”
verses.tsw_comparator: They say, “The LORD does not see; the God of Jacob does not perceive.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the challenge addressed within the people.
verses.before: Understand, you senseless among the people; you fools, when will you become wise?
verses.after: Understand, you senseless ones among the people! You fools, when will you grow wise?
verses.tsw_comparator: Understand, you senseless among the people; you fools, when will you become wise?

verses.rationale: Preserves planted ear and formed eye as creation arguments.
verses.before: The One who planted the ear—does God not hear? The One who formed the eye—does God not see?
verses.after: Does the one who planted the ear not hear? Does the one who formed the eye not see?
verses.tsw_comparator: The One who planted the ear—does God not hear? The One who formed the eye—does God not see?

verses.rationale: Keeps the unfinished appositional structure without inventing a third question.
verses.before: The One who disciplines nations—does God not rebuke? The One who teaches humankind—does God not know?
verses.after: Does the one who disciplines nations not correct— the one who teaches human beings knowledge?
verses.tsw_comparator: The One who disciplines nations—does God not rebuke? The One who teaches humankind—does God not know?

verses.rationale: Retains breath as the image of futility and transience.
verses.before: The LORD knows human thoughts, that they are only breath.
verses.after: The LORD knows human thoughts: they are only a breath.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD knows human thoughts, that they are only breath.

verses.rationale: Keeps YAH and the instructional purpose of discipline.
verses.before: Happy is the one whom you discipline, O LORD, and whom you teach from your instruction,
verses.after: How fortunate is the person you discipline, YAH, the one you teach from your instruction,
verses.tsw_comparator: Happy is the one whom you discipline, O LORD, and whom you teach from your instruction,

verses.rationale: Preserves temporal until and the reversal awaiting the wicked.
verses.before: to give that one rest from days of trouble, until a pit is dug for the wicked.
verses.after: giving relief from days of trouble until a pit is dug for the wicked.
verses.tsw_comparator: to give that one rest from days of trouble, until a pit is dug for the wicked.

verses.rationale: Retains paired nonabandonment promises.
verses.before: For the LORD will not abandon the people or forsake the inheritance.
verses.after: For the LORD will not cast off his people or abandon his inheritance.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the LORD will not abandon the people or forsake the inheritance.

verses.rationale: Keeps restored justice and the responsive upright community.
verses.before: For judgment will again accord with righteousness, and all the upright in heart will follow it.
verses.after: Judgment will again accord with righteousness, and all the upright in heart will follow it.
verses.tsw_comparator: For judgment will again accord with righteousness, and all the upright in heart will follow it.

verses.rationale: Preserves the personal plea and parallel rising/standing.
verses.before: Who rises up for me against the wicked? Who stands for me against people who do evil?
verses.after: Who will rise for me against evildoers? Who will take a stand for me against those who do wrong?
verses.tsw_comparator: Who rises up for me against the wicked? Who stands for me against those who do evil?

verses.rationale: Retains death's silence image rather than a direct substitution.
verses.before: If the LORD had not been my help, my soul would soon have dwelt in silence.
verses.after: If the LORD had not helped me, I would soon have made my home in silence.
verses.tsw_comparator: If the LORD had not been my help, my soul would soon have dwelt in silence.

verses.rationale: Keeps the bodily stumble and sustaining love.
verses.before: When I said, “My foot is slipping,” your steadfast love, O LORD, supported me.
verses.after: When I said, “My foot is slipping,” your faithful love, LORD, held me up.
verses.tsw_comparator: When I said, “My foot is slipping,” your steadfast love, O LORD, supported me.

verses.rationale: Retains inner multiplicity and consolation's enlivening effect.
verses.before: When my anxious thoughts were many within me, your consolations delighted my soul.
verses.after: When anxious thoughts crowded within me, your consolations brought me joy.
verses.tsw_comparator: When my anxious thoughts were many within me, your consolations delighted my soul.

verses.rationale: Preserves institutional wrongdoing through law without modern political insertion.
verses.before: Can a throne of destruction be allied with you— one that frames injustice by statute?
verses.after: Can a throne of destruction be allied with you, one that uses law to fashion misery?
verses.tsw_comparator: Can a throne of destruction be allied with you— one that frames injustice by statute?

verses.rationale: Keeps deadly conspiracy and judicial condemnation.
verses.before: They band together against the life of the righteous and condemn innocent blood.
verses.after: They band together against the life of the righteous and condemn innocent blood.
verses.tsw_comparator: They band together against the life of the righteous and condemn innocent blood.

verses.rationale: Retains both defensive images and personal assurance.
verses.before: But the LORD has become my stronghold, and my God the rock of my refuge.
verses.after: But the LORD has become my stronghold; my God is the rock where I take refuge.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the LORD has become my stronghold, and my God the rock of my refuge.

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated severe ending and their evil's recoil.
verses.before: God will bring their iniquity back upon them and destroy them by their own evil; the LORD our God will destroy them.
verses.after: He will turn their wrongdoing back on them and destroy them through their own evil. The LORD our God will destroy them.
verses.tsw_comparator: God will bring their iniquity back upon them and destroy them by their own evil; the LORD our God will destroy them.

verses.rationale: Keeps communal invitation and the rock title.
verses.before: Come—let us sing to the LORD; let us shout with joy to the rock of our salvation.
verses.after: Come, let us sing for joy to the LORD; let us shout to the rock of our salvation.
verses.tsw_comparator: Come—let us sing to the LORD; let us shout with joy to the rock of our salvation.

verses.rationale: Retains thanksgiving and repeated acclamation.
verses.before: Let us come before the LORD with thanksgiving; let us make a joyful noise with songs of praise.
verses.after: Let us come before him with thanksgiving and shout to him with songs.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let us come before the LORD with thanksgiving; let us make a joyful noise with songs of praise.

verses.rationale: Preserves the stated comparison and doubled greatness.
verses.before: For the LORD is a great God, and a great king above all gods.
verses.after: For the LORD is a great God, a great king above all gods.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the LORD is a great God, and a great king above all gods.

verses.rationale: Keeps vertical extremes under divine ownership.
verses.before: In the LORD’s hand are the depths of the earth; the heights of the mountains also belong to the LORD.
verses.after: The depths of the earth are in his hand; the mountain heights belong to him.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the LORD’s hand are the depths of the earth; the heights of the mountains also belong to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains sea/land contrast and forming hands.
verses.before: The sea is the LORD’s, for the LORD made it, and the dry land, which the LORD’s hands formed.
verses.after: The sea is his, for he made it; his hands formed the dry land.
verses.tsw_comparator: The sea is the LORD’s, for the LORD made it, and the dry land, which the LORD’s hands formed.

verses.rationale: Preserves embodied worship and human creation.
verses.before: Come—let us bow down and worship; let us kneel before the LORD, our maker.
verses.after: Come, let us bow down in worship; let us kneel before the LORD who made us.
verses.tsw_comparator: Come—let us bow down and worship; let us kneel before the LORD, our maker.

verses.rationale: Keeps people/flock imagery and the transition into the warning.
verses.before: For the LORD is our God, and we are the people of the LORD’s pasture, and the sheep of the LORD’s hand. Today, if you hear the LORD’s voice,
verses.after: For he is our God, and we are the people of his pasture, the flock in his hand. Today, if you hear his voice,
verses.tsw_comparator: For the LORD is our God, and we are the people of the LORD’s pasture, and the sheep of the LORD’s hand. Today, if you hear the LORD’s voice,

verses.rationale: Retains both place names and marks the divine voice.
verses.before: do not harden your hearts, as at Meribah, as on the day at Massah in the wilderness,
verses.after: “Do not harden your hearts as at Meribah, as on the day of Massah in the wilderness,
verses.tsw_comparator: do not harden your hearts, as at Meribah, as on the day at Massah in the wilderness,

verses.rationale: Keeps the testing verbs and prior sight of divine action.
verses.before: where your ancestors tested me, they tried me, though they had seen my work.
verses.after: where your fathers tested me and put me to the proof, though they had seen my work.
verses.tsw_comparator: where your ancestors tested me, they tried me, though they had seen my work.

verses.rationale: Retains exact forty and the force of divine aversion.
verses.before: For forty years I was weary of that generation, and I said, “They are a people whose hearts go astray, and they do not know my ways.”
verses.after: For forty years I loathed that generation. I said, ‘Their hearts keep straying; they do not know my ways.’
verses.tsw_comparator: For forty years I was weary of that generation, and I said, “They are a people whose hearts go astray, and they do not know my ways.”

verses.rationale: Renders the oath's negative force explicitly without importing a later destination.
verses.before: So I swore in my anger, “They will not enter my rest.”
verses.after: So I swore in my anger, ‘They will never enter my rest.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore I swore in my anger, “They shall not enter my rest.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the first two calls to sing and worldwide scope.
verses.before: Sing to the LORD a new song; sing to the LORD, all the earth!
verses.after: Sing a new song to the LORD; sing to the LORD, all the earth!
verses.tsw_comparator: Sing to the LORD a new song; sing to the LORD, all the earth!

verses.rationale: Retains the third sing and repeated daily proclamation.
verses.before: Sing to the LORD, bless his name; proclaim his salvation from day to day.
verses.after: Sing to the LORD; bless his name. Day after day, announce his salvation.
verses.tsw_comparator: Sing to the LORD, bless his name; proclaim his salvation from day to day.

verses.rationale: Keeps nations/peoples and glory/wonders in parallel.
verses.before: Declare his glory among the nations, his wondrous works among all peoples!
verses.after: Tell the nations of his glory, all the peoples of his wonders.
verses.tsw_comparator: Declare his glory among the nations, his wondrous works among all peoples!

verses.rationale: Retains greatness and fearful comparison without diminishing either.
verses.before: For great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised; he is to be feared above all gods.
verses.after: For the LORD is great and greatly to be praised; he is to be feared above all gods.
verses.tsw_comparator: For great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised; he is to be feared above all gods.

verses.rationale: Makes the elohim/elilim contrast intelligible while noting the Hebrew wordplay.
verses.before: For all the gods of the peoples are idols, but the LORD made the heavens.
verses.after: All the gods of the peoples are worthless idols, but the LORD made the heavens.
verses.tsw_comparator: For all the gods of the peoples are idols, but the LORD made the heavens.

verses.rationale: Preserves the four attributes and sacred setting.
verses.before: Splendor and majesty are before him; strength and beauty are in his sanctuary.
verses.after: Splendor and majesty are before him; strength and beauty fill his sanctuary.
verses.tsw_comparator: Splendor and majesty are before him; strength and beauty are in his sanctuary.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated ascription and extended human families.
verses.before: Ascribe to the LORD, O families of the peoples, ascribe to the LORD glory and strength!
verses.after: Ascribe to the LORD, families of the peoples, ascribe to the LORD glory and strength.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ascribe to the LORD, O families of the peoples, ascribe to the LORD glory and strength!

verses.rationale: Keeps third ascription and concrete offering.
verses.before: Ascribe to the LORD the glory due his name; bring an offering and come into his courts!
verses.after: Ascribe to the LORD the glory of his name; bring an offering and enter his courts.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ascribe to the LORD the glory due his name; bring an offering and come into his courts!

verses.rationale: Preserves ambiguous holy splendor with attire alternative in note.
verses.before: Worship the LORD in the splendor of holiness; tremble before him, all the earth!
verses.after: Bow before the LORD in holy splendor; tremble before him, all the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: Worship the LORD in the splendor of holiness; tremble before him, all the earth!

verses.rationale: Keeps reign, world stability and fair judgment together.
verses.before: Say among the nations, “The LORD reigns! Indeed, the world is established—it will not be moved; he will judge the peoples with equity.”
verses.after: Say among the nations, “The LORD reigns! The world stands firm; it cannot be shaken. He will judge the peoples fairly.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Say among the nations, “The LORD reigns! Indeed, the world is established—it shall not be moved; he will judge the peoples with equity.”

verses.rationale: Retains nonhuman creation's praise and sea fullness.
verses.before: Let the heavens be glad, and let the earth rejoice; let the sea roar, and all that fills it;
verses.after: Let the heavens be glad and the earth rejoice; let the sea thunder with everything in it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let the heavens be glad, and let the earth rejoice; let the sea roar, and all that fills it;
